Ford Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by Matthew Visinsky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Steve Helwick · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Time and date: Friday, November 6 at 7:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-6) Over/under: 56.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 2-1 Last meeting: SMU 28, Virginia Tech 25 — September 21, 1974 Current streak: SMU, 2 (1973-74) Setting the scene While No. 1 Miami (FL) and No. 14 Wake Forest are the only ACC teams that reside in the AP Top 25, the conference title race is far from finished. There are five two-loss teams lurking right behind, and two of them clash Friday night in Dallas. It's the first meeting between SMU and Virginia Tech as ACC opponents, however, it's a familiar head coaching matchup: Rhett Lashlee and James Franklin stood on opposite sidelines as recently as 2024 in the College Football Playoff. There's plenty on the line for the bowl eligible opponents. A win would do wonders for remaining in the ACC race, especially for SMU, which can still capture a tiebreaker against Wake Forest. But a third conference loss is essentially an elimination in a 17-team league. Virginia Tech Hokies outlook BLACKSBURG, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 17: Head coach James Franklin of the Virginia Tech Hokies greets Kaleb Spencer #3 before the game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets at Lane Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Blacksburg, Virginia. (Photo by Michael Shroyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) can make another statement on the road after its bye week. The Hokies haven't rattled off seven wins in a regular season since 2019, but that streak could end Friday in year one of the James Franklin era. Virginia Tech is fresh off its biggest win under Franklin, taking down Clemson 20-16 in Death Valley on Oct. 24. Close games have been commonplace for the Hokies this season. Each of their last six contests were decided by 10 points or fewer. Three featured lead changes in the final five minutes, while another ended on a missed field goal attempt that would have resulted in a lead change. The restoration of Virginia Tech football can be attributed to the passing game. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer followed Franklin from Penn State and has drastically improved in his junior campaign. Grunkemeyer has connected on an efficient 71.4 percent of attempts — seventh nationally among quarterbacks with 100 attempts — and has delivered 17 touchdowns against two interceptions. Grunkemeyer has eclipsed 300 yards three times and finished seven of his eight starts without throwing a pick. Two receivers have carried a bulk of the load. Wide receiver Que'Sean Brown ranks atop the team with 51 receptions and 685 receiving yards, and he's secured at least five receptions in all eight games. Tight end Luke Reynolds has also been a matchup nightmare for defenses. Reynolds' 50 receptions rank first and his 491 receiving yards ranks third among all FBS tight ends. While a bulk of his production occurred in September, his outing against Clemson was a productive one, snagging two touchdowns on seven receptions. The Hokies aren't as adept in the run game, where they check in at 111th in the FBS with 3.7 yards per carry. They don't incorporate much quarterbaack mobility and primarily rely on the duo of Jeffrey Overton Jr. and Marcellous Hawkins Jr. Overton, a common weapon in the receiving game, showed the extent of his powers in a 209-yard rushing explosion against Boston College. Hawkins has been a steady secondary back, and he's tied for the team lead with five rushing touchdowns. Virginia Tech only surrendered more than 26 points once this season, and that was a Friday night matchup against Pittsburgh. The Hokies' defense has been a positive for the team, tied for 35th in points allowed and ranked 27th in yards allowed per game. Their strength involves limiting the run, where they give up just 93.4 yards per game on a 3.0 average. Sacks heavily factor into that total, and Virginia Tech is the best in the ACC and the sixth-best in the nation at getting to the quarterback, producing 3.4 sacks per game. It's a defensive end led effort. Aycen Stevens ranks first in the conference with 8.0 sacks, while his fellow defensive ends Cortez Harris and Mylachi Williams have 5.0 and 4.5, respectively. The Hokies haven't been as strong on the back end, but they prevent explosive plays well. No team has recorded a 50-yard completion on this defense all season. But what Virginia Tech needs to improve upon is its turnover output. The Hokies forced just five takeaways through eight games, causing the team to enter Friday with a minus-4 in the turnover battle this season. SMU Mustangs outlook DALLAS, TX - OCTOBER 17: Southern Methodist University Mustangs defensive end Marques White (16) rushes the passer during the game between SMU and Virginia on October 17, 2026 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by George Walker/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images SMU (6-2, 4-2 ACC) dropped from the rankings after a heartbreaking 30-27 loss at Syracuse last weekend. It was only the Mustangs' fourth conference defeat since joining the ACC, and the third in which they held a lead in the final minute. However, SMU has never lost back-to-back ACC games and owns an 11-0 record in ACC play at home, giving Rhett Lashlee's team the perfect opportunity to bounce back and remain in the conference title race. Slow starts have been the Mustangs' kryptonite. In their last five ACC games, they haven't scored more than 13 points in a half or entered the break with a lead larger than three. However, they've won each of their last five second halves, finishing a plus-68 over that span. SMU's offense is led by Kevin Jennings, who is one of seven passers averaging over 300 yards per game. This season has been a masterclass in efficiency for the senior, who is completing passes at a 73.7 percent clip — the third-highest rate in the country among quarterbacks with 100 attempts. Jennings has also thrown 152 consecutive passes without an interception, with his last misfire coming in the first quarter of a Sept. 26 matchup against Missouri State. The Mustangs' receiver room is as deep as they come, with five different players over the 200-yard threshold. Yamir Knight is the leader with 44 receptions for 523 yards, while Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale can also pose as explosive threats for an offense that ranks fifth nationally in 50+ yard receptions. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrstrom are also incorporated into the passing game, and they tie for the team lead with four receptions apiece. Unlike SMU's first ACC defeat at Louisville, last Saturday's loss to Syracuse was largely determined in the trenches. The Mustangs uncharacteristically allowed six sacks, accounting for 43 percent of their season total. Additionally, they struggled to create space for the running backs, which never broke off an explosive gain. Kendrick Raphael has posted three 100-yard games already in ACC play, and he can also do damage out of the backfield as a receiving option. SMU's defense didn't necessarily have a bad outing at Syracuse, limiting the Orange to 5.9 yards per passing attempt and 3.7 yards per rush. But the Mustangs surrendered conversions on all four of Syracuse's fourth down attempts, allowing the Orange to sustain otherwise lost drives. A veteran defensive line full of super seniors is the strength of the unit. SMU ranks 15th nationally with 2.9 sacks per game, and eighth-year senior Marques White leads the way with 5.5 sacks, while the rest of the sacks are quite evenly distributed. The pressure goes hand-in-hand with a strong passing defense, and SMU ranks 28th nationally in fewest passing yards allowed at 182 per game. That is the most improved element of the Mustangs from last year, but losing starting strong safety Tyren Polley for the year could make things difficult down the road. Sael Reyes stepped up last game with 10 tackles in his second start of the season, while Jimmy Wyrick recorded eight from the other safety spot. Lastly, turnovers have been a significant determinant in SMU results this season. The Mustangs lost the turnover battle 5-0 in their two losses, and they're the only bowl eligible team at a minus-5 or worse this season. These 6-2 teams are structured somewhat similarly: strong passing attacks with tight end utilization, dominant defensive fronts that repeatedly get to the quarterback, and solid defenses hampered by poor turnover margins. Short weeks oftentimes favor the home team, and SMU remains perfect against ACC opponents at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Given SMU's discrepancy between first and second half performance, Virginia Tech may enter halftime with the lead, but the Mustangs ultimately rally behind Kevin Jennings in the fourth quarter to secure a one-score win on The Hilltop. Prediction: SMU 30, Virginia Tech 24

picks.blurb: Virginia Tech Hokies vs. SMU Mustangs: News, Information, and Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Virginia Tech Hokies vs. SMU Mustangs: News, Information, and Predictions Stike up the Hokie Pokey, Tech Triumph, and the Victory Tag. | John Schneider - SB Nation John Schneider · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:59 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's a short week after a week break. The Hokies are heading to Dallas to face off against the Southern Methodist University Mustangs. The Hokies are up against another major ACC opponent, and winning the game means advancing in the ACC and potentially seeing a ranking. Crossover Week Mayhem Just a note from us: Well, the first week in November through the first week of December is always a challenge for coverage. The soccer teams are wrapping up with decent enough records, but their seasons aren't quite over. The Women's Basketball Team has opened their home record at 2-0, and the Men's team also graced Cassell with a W. All of that puts a real strain on coverage so bear with us as we sort out schedules, and fight fall health issues and work vs. Hokie sports balance. The football team isn't finished, though. There are still four games left on the schedule, and then we get to plan on bowl coverage this season. Isn't that a happy event? The Hokies are bowl eligible just a couple of games after the halfway point, and that's a very pleasant occurrence. To think that we are actually paying attention to the bowl invitation list, instead of worrying on Thanksgiving weekend whether or not a win will net an invitation somewhere. The first thing to cover is a bit of fun. The ACC Network desk hosts Eric McClain and Eddie Royal had a bet going. Remember, McClain is a former Clemson player, and we all know and love Eddie Royal. So, the bet was that the loser had to wear the winner's mascot costume. Eddie was not dressed as a Tiger with the googly eyes for the TV segment. ( Congratulations to the Virginia Tech Cheer Squad equipment folks and Travis Wells for getting most of an actual Hokie Bird big enough for Eric. ) The Virginia Tech Wrestling Team received a massive boost from a wrestler who hasn't even wrestled his first match as a Hokie, yet, but who is already a world champion. Freshman Bo Bassett traveled to Kazakhstan and netted the program its first world championship and was the first American in 20 years to win in his weight class (65KG – for those lacking metric conversion skills that's 143 pounds ). The Coach Robie is going to have an absolutely dominant wrestling team this season. Back to Football Stuff It looks like the team is going to be wearing head to toe all-whites for this one. Go get your coffee, or a quick snack and listen in on Coach Franklin's weekly presser. As Bryan posted up earlier, this time the Hokies have some really good news coming out of the locker room as it pertains to the Offensive Line. Montavious Cunningham and Brody Meadows are back up to speed and are expected to play on Friday night. The O-Line has been dipping into the #3s on the depth chart for the past few games, and getting them back is a serious update to the struggling run game. That All Leads to This… Predictions The SMU Mustangs are largely a Big XII import with a near automatic bubble to the top of the ACC football pile. It's Dallas, TX, and football is a near religion for Texas. That means the program is well funded, with premium coaching, and players doused liberally with NIL funding. Up until last weekend, the Mustangs were sporting a very respectable one loss record. Until they showed up in the Syracuse (whatever they call the Carrier Dome, now), as expected in the beginning of the season SMU was challenging hard for the #2 bid in the ACC fake Championship game ( until the conference goes back to divisions and division champs who play everyone else in the division the game in Charlotte will remain fake to me ). Then the Mustangs got treated to the old Big East upset win by the Orange. That knocked them down a peg but also put the Hokies in the position of earning the #3 spot on the ACC leader board. That all means that this game might not mean an ACC bid, but it will mean a much better bowl game situation over the holidays. Bowls mean big broadcast money, and the program needs the cash to make up for a restricted gate at Lane. The Mustangs are favored by slightly less than a touchdown for this one, in their house no less. We'll see how we feel about that. This is a big test for the Hokies. Virginia Tech had a huge win at Clemson two weeks ago. No, this isn't the same Clemson team as only a few years ago, but it means something for other ACC teams to walk into Death Valley and win. SMU is better than the Tigers, but they aren't unbeatable. The clear difference here is the quarterback position. SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings is a stud. He also has one of the ACC's best running backs and one of the top receiving units in the league. This is a huge challenge for VT defensive coordinator Brent Pry. Offensively, I think the Hokies have success moving the ball. SMU's size on the defensive interior concerns me, especially with Tech's OL struggles. There is hope that with Cunningham and Meadows back, the offensive line is better, but we'll see. I expect a close game. My heart says the Hokies, my head says SMU in a close one. SMU 34, Hokies 31 This game all depends on how the Mustangs adjusted to their Syracuse loss, and if the Hokies on both sides of the ball can adjust to how the Orange controlled the SMU offense, and how they managed to get by their defense. SMU, interestingly enough, has a similar offensive/defensive balance to Tech's than we have seen this season. There are lots of "IFs" in this game, and the biggest one is "IF" the Tech defense can limit the SMU offense to what it's been scoring over the season against peer teams, the Hokies have a much better chance to win than the listed 6-point betting gimme to SMU. The latest projected O/U is 56.5, which tells me volumes of information. The analysts see this as a very close game, and the end result being less than a full score between the two teams. If the Hokies stay away from getting enamored of the run game and go downfield fast and consistently in the air on quick developing intermediate routes to their best receivers, there will be run opportunities. If Tech decides to try to "establish the run" the offense could bog down into chronic 3-and-outs. The return of two key #1/#2 depth chart players is not an excuse to try to revert to 1960's caveman Johnny Unitas two runs and a pass offense. If the Hokies move the ball and do it fast, they have enough defense ( which needs to put serious pressure on the quarterback on every play ) to hold the Mustangs to a 3.5 score effort. The Hokies are capable of 4 or more. That's a whole lot of "Ifs" though. Here's the skinny… the first team to score over 30 points wins. That puts my prediction hat on, and I think the Hokies might just be good for it, regardless of the conditions. Just a quick reminder of the times and broadcast information. It's an ESPN deal.

According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Hokies enter as 6.5-point underdogs. Virginia Tech is 1-0 in its only game as an underdog, which was against Clemson on Oct. 24 in Clemson, S.C. The Hokies became bowl-eligible with their 20-16 win over the Tigers; quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's fourth-and-1 throw to tight end Luke Reynolds gave Virginia Tech a lead with 1:44 left it never relinquished. Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) opened its season with four straight wins for the first time since 2017, defeating VMI (73-3), Old Dominion (44-21), Maryland (35-26) , and Boston College ( 21-14) before its first loss came on Oct. 2 against Pitt. The Hokies got out to an early 14-0 lead over the Panthers but Tech conceded a 35-10 run that left it in an 11-point hole. Virginia Tech totaled nine points off a Davion "FatRat" Brown touchdown catch and a Noah Chambers safety, but fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal as time expired was ruled no good, resulting in a 35-33 loss to Pitt. Virginia Tech lost to Cal in Berkeley, Calif., the next week, scoring a season-low 20 points as its defense was sliced by Golden Bears backup Jackson Brousseau for 321 yards. That 321-yard total was the second-highest of Brousseau's career. The Hokies yielded a 14-play, 79-yard drive that elapsed just over seven minutes to Cal in the fourth quarter, giving the Golden Bears a 19-14 lead. And though Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown of its own with 1:15 left, Cal marched down the field in six plays and 75 yards - 30 of which arrived via penalty (roughing the passer, defensive pass interference). Virginia Tech drove down the field, setting up one final opportunity from Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining. However, Grunkemeyer's pass intended for Reynolds in the back of the end zone fell incomplete. The Hokies bounced back with a 34-24 win over Georgia Tech where they led 24-3 at intermission. Virginia Tech's four-point victory over Clemson affirmed its bowl aspirations, and the Hokies will travel to Dallas to take on SMU, which lost Saturday to Syracuse, 30-27. away.blurb: Starting left tackle Justin Terry is still progressing from an injury suffered against Maryland and has not been seen at practice, but guard/tackle Montavious Cunningham and guard Brody Meadows are ready to go. Meadows, a fifth-year player, returned against Clemson but played just four snaps, which is consistent with Franklin's comments Monday that there were weeks when the team expected him to be ready, only for him to be out or limited. "I don't think there's any doubt about it," Franklin said after practice Tuesday. "For me, part of the reason I'm in a little bit better mood tonight is having Montavious out at practice. The return of Cunningham and Meadows likely sends Troutman, Eziuka and Crawford back to the bench. While it's true that Cunningham has the worst PFF grade of the group (58.1), and Meadows' (66.0) is within three points of Troutman's (63.4) and Crawford's (66.5), that doesn't seem to paint the full picture. Practice Note: Cunningham and Meadows participated in most of the portion of Tuesday's practice open to media. Cornerback Thomas Williams, who didn't play against Clemson, participated and is questionable for Friday. Defensive lineman Emmett Laws is also questionable; he has yet to play this season. Terry was not seen at practice. 2. Theoretically, yes! Actually, this comment got me to look back at my notes from yesterday's practice. Virginia Tech vs. SMU: O-Line Returns, Plan for Kevin Jennings | The Key Play tag. --> Jump to navigation Montavious Cunningham and Brody Meadows are back for Friday's trip to SMU, and the defense has a plan for the most complete quarterback it has seen this season. After an incessant string of offensive line injuries early this season, head coach James Franklin and offensive line coach Matt Moore expect a near-full complement against SMU — as well as an overall upgrade in the unit's production. Franklin also noted that the team was still trying to find the best position for Cunningham. Regardless, expect to see some variation of guard/tackle Layth Ghannam, Meadows, center Kyle Altuner, Cunningham and tackle Aidan Lynch in Dallas. Ghannam is a natural guard, while Cunningham has played primarily tackle across six years of college football — though he hasn't played any snaps there this season. home.blurb: Starting left tackle Justin Terry is still progressing from an injury suffered against Maryland and has not been seen at practice, but guard/tackle Montavious Cunningham and guard Brody Meadows are ready to go. Here is how I'm wagering college football Week 10. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . No. 9 BYU @ No. 3 Utah This Holy War might be the holiest of them all: Utah hosting bitter rival BYU, with the winner in the driver's seat for a Playoff spot. It’s the first time both teams have been ranked in the top 10 for this matchup, and I can’t wait to start the day with this one. I think BYU might win outright. It has been tested with its win over Notre Dame just a few weeks ago. Yes, it lost to UCF the following week in a typical trap game — big home win followed by a road conference game. Otherwise, the Cougars have handled business, even though the scores don’t seem that impressive. BYU is built on defense. It is 13th in yards per play and it limits explosives. It does not rush the passer all that well, but against Utah’s rushing attack, that might not be needed. BYU’s defense already faced a high-powered offense in the Irish and limited it to a negative EPA rushing day. Utah’s offensive production slowly ticked down when conference play started, but it did bounce back last week against a poor Cincinnati defense. Utah has played one defense in the same realm as BYU and that was Houston. Utah struggled to score, only putting up 21 points with seven of those happening super late after forcing a Houston turnover. Will the BYU offense find a groove against Utah? (Getty Images) It’s fair to also believe BYU’s offense might struggle in this game. However, it appears the Cougars are getting stud running back LJ Martin back, and they are much better when Martin is on the field. He’s averaging almost eight yards a carry with 20% of his rushes going for 10+ yards. Utah’s defense is the typical physical front against the run, but BYU is the best offense the Utes have faced all season. Utah’s pass rush concerns me. It is 80th in pressure rate and unless it blitzes, it isn't able to get to the quarterback. Seems less than ideal against BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier. I see these teams as even. They are both defensively based with an offense that wants to run the ball. That’s too many points in a game like this. I’ll take BYU to cover. Schwartz's Pick: BYU -4.5 No. 5 Alabama @ No. 14 LSU In the newly-released CFP rankings, Alabama is fifth and is an underdog at LSU by almost a touchdown. I do lean towards LSU at -6, but that number feels big. Instead, I’m going to fade Alabama’s offense in this game. Alabama is facing its fourth straight difficult defense, and in the first three games, we’ve seen the offensive efficiency drop. Quarterback Keelon Russell is nearing the end of his first season as a starting quarterback, and he’s been mostly excellent for his age. However, he has struggled the last three weeks outside the end of the Texas A&M game. Against Georgia, Tennessee and A&M, he completed only 60% of passes with just four passing touchdowns and three interceptions. Alabama’s beat-up offensive line has allowed 11 sacks in the three previous games. Now, the Tide play an LSU defense that’s first in sacks per pressure and 11th in pressure rate. The Bama offensive line and Russell were noticeably affected by the environment in Tennessee, and now they are at LSU. I feel most comfortable with Alabama not scoring much in this game. away.blurb: On Wednesday night, the BYU football program provided the first official injury update for LJ Martin ahead of a top 10 matchup with Utah. Martin is "doubtful" for the game against the Utes. The "doubtful" designation is reserved for the players that have a 25% chance to play. However, just a few minutes before the injury report came out, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Martin is considered "questionable" for this weekend. The "questionable" designation is reserved for players with a 50% chance to play. Thamel reported that if Martin returns, "he's not expected to be 100% and could be limited." Thamel added more information, saying "[Martin is] trending to dress, be available, and have some impact on the game. A final decision will be made later this week." Martin was back practicing on Tuesday, according to Aaron Roderick. The last time he played was in early October against TCU. If Martin can't go, BYU will turn to Preston Rex who was not available for the ASU game. Rex had a breakout game against Notre Dame before suffering an injury against UCF. If Saleapaga isn't available, expect more sets with three wide receivers. That would leave Walker Lyons on the field for most of the game. If Evan Johnson can't play, BYU will turn to Jayven Williams and Therrian Alexander III at cornerback. Williams and Alexander shut down two of the best wide receivers in the Big 12 last week. They are more than capable of holding it down on the outside. The bigger question will be who BYU plays at nickel. The Cougars started Cannon DeVries at that spot to start the season, but DeVries has primarily been used for punt return duties since he suffered an injury. The ASU game was the first time DeVries had seen defensive snaps since suffering the injury. He played 14 snaps. LJ Martin and Evan Johnson Officially Ruled Out for BYU Against ASU If Martin returns, it would be the first time BYU has had its full compliment of running backs since the season opener. Saleapaga left the game against ASU with an injury, and Johnson suffered what appeared to be a serious ankle injury against UCF. Johnson did not play against Arizona State last weekend. Most of the time, BYU had three safeties on the field. BYU averaged 2.7 safeties on the field at a time against ASU. True freshman Kennan Pula has seen his role grow over the last few weeks. The Tigers (6-2, 3-2 SEC) have already blown out league foes Florida and Texas A&M at home this season and are 13-3 at Faurot Field against league opposition since 2023. Taking on Texas (6-2, 3-2) represents an uptick in competition, but the Tigers shouldn't be lacking confidence. Florida was No. 8 in the AP poll when it arrived at Mizzou on Oct. 3. It left with a 45-17 loss that legitimized Missouri and showed its full potential. Since then, we've also seen Missouri's floor, which was found in a 31-3 loss at Ole Miss on Oct. 17. But after a bye week and a 34-10 "get right" win over Arkansas in Week 9, the Tigers appear to be back on track. The Longhorns are entering off wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State , but their vaunted offense is still falling short of expectations. Is this the point when everything will start to click for quarterback Arch Manning ? If a Texas team that spent four weeks at No. 1 earlier this season is going to meet expectations, a breakthrough needs to come soon. Texas vs. Missouri: Need to know Injuries mount for Texas: Injuries are adding up for the Longhorns, who enter this matchup with star receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman listed as questionable. Wingo is dealing with a quad injury while Coleman is working through a shoulder issue. Both have appeared in all eight games for Texas up to this point while combining to catch 11 of Arch Manning's 15 touchdown passes. Star edge rusher Collin Simmons is also questionable after missing Texas' past two games because of an ankle injury. That's a lot of star power in the "questionable" category for Texas. By contrast, Missouri's injury report is nearly clean. Welcome back, Ahmad: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy made his 2026 debut last week, carrying the football twice in the Tigers' win over Arkansas. The 2025 All-American has been on the mend from a gunshot wound, and his return adds to a running back room that already features the SEC's leading rusher. Jamal Roberts became the conference's first back to surpass 1,000 yards for the season while rushing for 138 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in a win over Arkansas. Roberts surpassed 200 yards in wins over Florida and Texas A&M last month. Gaining traction against Texas will be tough. No team has averaged more than four yards per rush attempt against Texas. College Football playoff implications: Texas' chance to reach the College Football Playoff will improve to 67.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFB Forecaster. They will drop to 22.8% with a loss. If the Longhorns lose, they would need to win out against LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M in order to potentially reach the 12-team field as a three-loss team. Missouri's chances to make the CFP will improve to 16.1% with a win. Those hopes would crater to 1.6% with a loss. The Tigers close with Georgia , Kentucky and Oklahoma . Regardless of the health status of star edge rusher Collin Simmons, the Longhorns should be able to slow down a Missouri offense that hasn't faced a swarming unit of this caliber. If Arch Manning can just take care of the football like he did last week, Texas can lean on its defense, win the field position battle and put stress on a Missouri defense that showed real vulnerability in losses to Mississippi State and Ole Miss. The Tigers have been great at home the last few years, but they are a rung below Texas in overall talent level. Staff Picks and Scores Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB After getting to play their entire October slate in the Lone Star State, the Longhorns are once again leaving town for Columbia, Missouri, to take on the No. 18 Missouri Tigers. While fans may already be looking ahead to next week's highly anticipated Death Valley matchup, the Tigers are certainly not a team to overlook . They're coming off a 34-10 blowout win over Arkansas — albeit, it was against the Razorbacks — and steamrolled the same Florida team that stunned Texas with a second-half comeback just a few weeks ago. Saturday's matchup carries significant postseason implications , both for the College Football Playoff and the SEC championship race, as both teams enter with identical 3-2 conference records. Here’s how the Texas Longhorns On SI Staff sees this one playing out. Matt Galatzan Texas has gotten back on track over the last two weeks, but various shortcoming are still very prevelent. Texas has struggled along offensive line, and as a result, the running game has suffered. Those issues have also caused a cascading effect on the passing game, making for an inconsistent product. To make things worse, things on the injury front don't look good for the Horns. Kade Phillips, Ryan Wingo and Graceson Littleton are all banged up but should play, while Colin Simmons and Cam Coleman are less likely to play, and Hollywood Smothers and Nick Townsend were both lost for the year. Texas can overcome these issues if the defense continues to perform at a high level. Ole Miss showed the blueprint to shut down the Tigers ' offense. If Texas can stay on schedule on offense and avoid a third-quarter collapse, I think they can get it done. Texas 27, Missouri 20 Phoenix Haigis Texas has started to find their groove again with two major wins at home against Ole Miss and Mississippi State. The Longhorns now go back on the road against another ranked opponent in Missouri. As much momentum as Texas has going into this game, all the advantages matchup-wise go in favor of the Tigers. Texas is dealing with a significant amount of major injuries with the addition of running back Hollywood Smothers being out for the season while Missouri will see their running back Ahmad Hardy return for the first time this season. The Tigers are one of the best teams at home this year and have the best turnover margin in the SEC against a Lorghorns team that has had turnover issues this season. Although Texas is favored, the math tells a different story and could eliminate the Longhorns’ playoff chances. Zion Trammell Texas and Missouri have the makings of a defensive slugfest. It’ll be a cold morning in Columbia, Missouri, which could challenge the offenses. Both the Longhorns and Tigers rank in the top four in the SEC in average rushing yards allowed per game. Texas may need a big defensive play to win. I think Will Muschamp’s defense will deliver, and the Longhorns will win a close game on Saturday. However, this feels like the Arch legacy game that many have been begging to see. Perhaps it's also because that might be what HAS to happen, but I'm riding with believing in Manning in this one. It won't be pretty, and it might even be a little boring at times — that is, if all you care about is high-flying action. And while the injury report isn't promising one bit, I still believe this Texas defense can be every bit as legitimate as it's proven itself to be. Stopping Missouri starts with shutting down the run game, and I fully expect Justin Cryer and Rasheem Biles to help answer the call. I could easily see either one leading the team in tackles by the time it's all said and done. Ultimately, Texas' ability to stonewall opposing offenses should be enough to keep the Tigers in check, giving its sometimes-average offense just enough breathing room to squeak out another win. picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Predicts Missouri Upset That Could Shake Texas' Playoff Hopes Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy believes Texas’ turnover problems will catch up with the Longhorns at Missouri, making the Tigers his lone outright upset pick of Week 10 as both 6-2 SEC teams fight to stay in the College Football Playoff race. McElroy backed the Tigers on his Always College Football podcast, predicting a low-scoring game decided by ball security. “The team that gives it away just one time, that’s the team that’s going to lose,” he said. Why is Greg McElroy picking Missouri? Missouri Tigers head coach Eli Drinkwitz reacts toward a referee during the first quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “Missouri is +8 in turnover margin. Texas is -3,” McElroy said. “That’s probably the clearest season-long difference between these two teams.” “Missouri is +8 in turnover margin. Texas is -3,” McElroy said. “That’s probably the clearest season-long difference between these two teams.” The Tigers turned four Arkansas turnovers into 24 points in last week’s win in Fayetteville, and Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz said afterward that “turnovers are the name of the game .” McElroy added that Missouri has scored 62 points off takeaways this season without allowing a point off a giveaway. “So when his team wins the turnover battle by one or more, Eli Drinkwitz is 39-4,” McElroy said. Texas checked in at No. 7 in the first College Football Playoff rankings , 11 spots ahead of Missouri. Still, both Missouri losses came on the road against Mississippi State and Ole Miss, two teams Texas beat over the last two weeks. Arch Manning’s costly turnover trouble Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) looks on after a medical check during the game against Ole Miss | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Texas quarterback Arch Manning has 15 touchdown passes and averages 8 yards per attempt, but McElroy flagged his seven interceptions as a problem against a team that “cashes mistakes in very, very quickly.” Both Texas losses came by three points and turned on fourth-quarter turnovers, including a pick-six against Oklahoma and a strip-sack with under two minutes left against Florida. Texas quarterback Arch Manning has 15 touchdown passes and averages 8 yards per attempt, but McElroy flagged his seven interceptions as a problem against a team that “cashes mistakes in very, very quickly.” Both Texas losses came by three points and turned on fourth-quarter turnovers, including a pick-six against Oklahoma and a strip-sack with under two minutes left against Florida. Mississippi State sacked the redshirt junior six times last Saturday, and Texas now plays without left tackle Trevor Goosby, who suffered a season-ending knee injury against Ole Miss. “They average getting sacked nearly one out of every 10 dropbacks,” McElroy said of Texas. “That’s 126th because the breakdowns come from all over the protection.” The ESPN analyst said Texas has struggled when its receivers have to beat man coverage snap after snap, and he called Missouri’s cornerbacks “about as good as you find when it comes to playing that coverage week in and week out.” How does Texas reach 24 points? Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian celebrates with fans and players after the game against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy questioned how Texas coach Steve Sarkisian’s offense gets there. “When his team scores fewer than 24 points, Steve Sarkisian is 14-35,” McElroy said. “And Texas already goes three-and-out on more than a quarter of their possessions.” McElroy questioned how Texas coach Steve Sarkisian’s offense gets there. “When his team scores fewer than 24 points, Steve Sarkisian is 14-35,” McElroy said. “And Texas already goes three-and-out on more than a quarter of their possessions.” The Longhorns’ running game offers little relief, with McElroy saying their backs “are getting hit almost as soon as they take the handoff.” Running back Hollywood Smothers is out, and receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman were both listed as questionable on Thursday’s SEC availability report . Wingo, a St. Louis native Missouri recruited out of high school, leads Texas with 36 catches for 470 yards, while Coleman, an Auburn transfer, leads the team with seven touchdown catches. McElroy’s route to 24 points runs through Wingo “in the catch-and-run game” against a Missouri defense he said sits “at or near the bottom as far as missed tackles,” plus “one Coleman shot over the top.” “But without it, Texas might be living on field goals, which is a dangerous recipe on the road,” McElroy said. A loss would send Texas to LSU next week with three defeats, a scenario ESPN analyst Paul Finebaum said could cause the Longhorns to “ collapse .” Texas visits Missouri at noon ET Saturday on ESPN. picks.blurb: Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas vs. Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas vs. Missouri Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 7 Texas and No. 18 Missouri have only met once on the football field since the Tigers left the Big 12 along side Texas A&M for the SEC. That meeting was the 2017 Texas Bowl. What should scare Longhorns fans is the 2026 version is tinkering on the edge of a disappointing bowl like that. Especially if they can't beat a team like Missouri. The Tigers are a good team. It's easy to see Missouri winning on Saturday. They're ranked just 11 spots below Texas in the College Football Playoff rankings and have the same record. And Mizzou has home field advantage. Then why is Texas a -3.5-point favorite. Because a fully functioning Texas team is better than Missouri. But this Texas team isn't fully functioning. First, the injuries are starting to pile up. It was announced this week that the Longhorns have lost running back Hollywood Smothers and tight end Nick Townsend for the rest of the season. All-American right tackle Trevor Goosby is also out for the year. And UT has been without All-American EDGE Colin Simmons for weeks. In addition to trying to plug the injury holes, Texas coach Steve Sarkisian must also continue to work on the offense. At times it looks great. But its not trustworthy. Will Muschamp's defense will need to stand tall for a third game in a row if the offense can't get it going. Tommy Bresee's Prediction Texas walks into this Missouri game needing the win to feel confident about their CFP chance heading into LSU. Missouri is a relative unknown, with losses to both Mississippi schools but a dominating win over Florida. Jamal Roberts and the run game leads the way, averaging just over 160 rushing yards/game. Austin Simmons has become a riser in this upcoming NFL Draft, flashing his elite arm talent every week. Texas was able to get a win over Tennessee earlier this season, but I don't see this as a task that's comparable. Missouri is capable of performing at a high level on both sides of the ball, especially the front seven defensively. It's difficult to imagine this Texas offense to trade punches with Missouri, especially on the road, so I'll take the Tigers to possibly end Texas' CFP hopes. Final Score: Texas 20, Missouri 23 Jamie Gatlin's Prediction The Longhorns will take on Missouri this Saturday in their latest SEC clash. The Tigers are off to an impressive 6-2 start and, like Texas, are 3-2 in conference play. Texas will need Arch Manning to be at his best and for the defense to shine. Last week, the Longhorns defense held Mississippi State to three points and 187 total yards. If the Longhorns can replicate that performance, another win could be on the horizon. This should be a game that Texas can win as they look to improve their playoff odds. Final Score: Texas 31, Missouri 13 Trey Luerssen's Prediction When this year's schedule came out, I thought the game against Mizzou might be the toughest to forecast. But it's even tougher now, because we're not sure which team will actually show up on either side of the ball. Both teams have had some big wins and some real clunkers. How much will Texas miss Smothers and Townsend? Can the defense slow down the Tigers offense? Which version of quarterback Arch Manning will show up in Columbia? For four games in a row, Texas has jumped out to an early lead and then coughed it up by the end of the third quarter. UT is 2-2 in that stretch. A coin flip. Twice the dam broke and twice it didn't. I think the defense will save the offense again. Texas vs Missouri Odds, Point Spread, Betting Lines Texas vs Missouri Spread : Texas -2.5, Missouri +2.5 Texas vs Missouri Over/Under : 43.5 Total Points Texas vs Missouri Moneyline : Texas ML -135, Missouri ML +114 Even in a win over Mississippi State , the celebrations for Texas were cut short with Cam Coleman , Ryan Wingo and Hollywood Smothers all going down with injuries against the Bulldogs. That was a devastating result after Trevor Goosby — a pillar of the Longhorns' offensive line who is projected to be a top-10 pick in next year's draft — had already been ruled out for the remainder of the year. The injuries for Texas could be the straw that breaks the camel's back, with the Longhorns already struggling on offense, limping into Week 10 ranked 74th in Success Rate, 95th in Explosiveness and 129th in Havoc Allowed. Arch Manning's inconsistencies have made it difficult for Texas to stay ahead of the sticks, leaving the offense vulnerable to stalling out early on in drives. While Coleman and Wingo are expected to play at less than 100%, Smothers' outlook looks bleak, forcing the Longhorns to lean more heavily on Raleek Brown . When given the opportunity, Brown has been a consistent source of production in the Texas backfield, averaging nearly five yards per carry. With question marks lingering over the offense, the Longhorns will need to continue to play at a high level on the other side of the ball in order to keep their hopes of making the playoffs alive. Luckily for Texas, the defense has been the strength of the team this season, entering Week 10 ranked in the top 25 in Success Rate, Explosiveness, Finishing Drives and Havoc. Missouri 's hot start to the year is arguably one of the bigger surprises of the season, with the Tigers just one win away from clearing the over on their regular-season win total while sitting 1.5 games back from first in the SEC conference standings. Austin Simmons ' resurgence under center has played a major role in Missouri's success, throwing just two interceptions in eight games while averaging 8.1 yards per throw. While Simmons has been able to thrive through the air, the Tigers' running back room has yet to find its footing, ranking near the bottom of the board in Rush Success Rate and PPA. When Jamal Roberts is unable to hit the ground running, opposing defenses can stretch out their linebackers across the middle, smothering Simmons' passing lanes at multiple levels of the field. It is worth noting Ahmad Hardy was able to make his return to the field after suffering a scary gunshot wound in the offseason, potentially giving Missouri the spark it needs to be a well-rounded offense. While his return was welcome to see, expectations will need to be tempered, with the Tigers' running back being held to just two carries. Like Texas, Missouri has also built its success on the shoulders of the defense, fielding a group that ranks 29th in Success Rate and fifth in Havoc. While the Tigers do give up explosive plays at an alarming rate, they are able to successfully keep their opponents out of the end zone, giving up just 3.03 Points per Opportunity. While Simmons has been able to play far better than initially expected, negative regression is looming large over the Tigers' quarterback as he battles it out against a secondary that excels in coverage, per its top-30 mark in Dropback EPA Allowed per play. With the Longhorns keeping a body on Missouri's pass-catchers' hips, the amount of Havoc in Simmons' throws will increase, leading to an uptick in his total number of Turnover-Worthy Plays. Even with Hardy back on the field, it's tough to envision the star running back being able to quickly shake off the rust, making the Tigers far too one-dimensional. Barring a sudden turnaround on the ground, Texas will be able to drop more bodies back in coverage, making it easier to create disruptions. Colin Simmons has also been upgraded to questionable, yet it remains to be seen if the Longhorns' edge rusher will suit up on Saturday. While the Longhorns do generate pressure at a high rate, Simmons would help pull defensive attention to the edge, freeing up more space in the interior to help the middle of the defensive line collapse the pocket. With no clear path for success, expect Missouri to be held to early outs at a consistent rate, chipping away at the Tigers' total number of scoring opportunities. away.headline: Texas' Hollywood Smothers Reportedly Out for Rest of CFB Season with Knee Injury
away.blurb: Smothers wasn't available for games against Tennessee and Ole Miss, and he has been an ineffective option as part of a rotation with running back Raleek Brown. Smothers carried the ball just four times for minus-6 yards before entering the medical tent against Mississippi State last week. Texas running back Hollywood Smothers will miss the remainder of the 2026 season with a torn MCL, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported. Smothers was among the top running backs in the 2026 transfer class after rushing for 939 yards with seven touchdowns at NC State last season. He was expected to be an explosive addition to the Longhorns offense and began the season as the starting running back, but he has been hampered by injuries throughout the season. The Longhorns entered the season with high expectations, but inconsistent performances from quarterback Arch Manning and a bevy of injuries have threatened to derail their campaign. Texas was ranked No. 1 after starting the season with a 4-0 record, but they now sit as the No. 7 ranked team after two consecutive losses against unranked Oklahoma and Florida. Texas will need Brown to carry a larger workload as they fight to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive moving forward, but the injuries are continuing to mount. The Longhorns have already lost star left tackle Trevor Goosby to a season-ending injury, and the team's injury report for their upcoming game against Missouri is nearly as long as a drug store receipt. Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian will need players to step up in order for the team to live up to their preseason expectations. The margin for error is slim, and those injuries could prove to be critical during their upcoming road games against two ranked opponents, No. 18 Missouri and No. 14 LSU. away.blurb: The final injury report released Friday night shed some light on the status of some key Texas players, including multiple starters. The good news? Multiple players were upgraded to probable, but the bad news is that the status of two others remained unchanged. UPGRADED TO PROBABLE: CB Kade Phillips, WR Ryan Wingo, CB Graceson Littleton REMAINS QUESTIONABLE: DE Colin Simmons, WR Cam Coleman RULED OUT: RB Hollywood Smothers, OL Trevor Goosby, TE Nick Townsend, DE Richard Wesley According to ESPN's Pete Thamel, Simmons traveled with the team to Columbia and will test out his ankle injury during pregame warmups. If he plays, Simmons is expected to be on a pitch count. It truly looks like he will be a game-time decision. Simmons has missed the past two games and the expectation was that he could return against Missouri but that remains to be seen. The Longhorns will continue to lean on Wingo and Mosley moving forward if Coleman is officially ruled out against Mizzou and beyond. So far this season, Coleman has tallied 23 catches for 409 yards and seven touchdowns. 5 Texas Starters Questionable on Initial Injury Report vs. Missouri The Texas Longhorns are dealing with some major injury questions before visiting Missouri in Columbia on Saturday. Coleman suffered an upper-body injury in the first half during the win over Mississippi State. He returned to the sideline with a sling on his left arm/shoulder. Per Thamel's report, there is not a ton of optimism that Coleman will play against Missouri. Though Coleman is arguably Texas' most talented receiver, the production hasn't quite matched that. He's the team's third-leading receiver behind Wingo and Emmett Mosley despite playing in all eight games this season. Steve Sarkisian Confident If Other Players Need to Step Up If Littleton or Phillips are unable to play, freshman cornerback Samari Matthews would be one of the players expected to step up. Should that happen, Sarkisian is confident in what he brings to the table. "Samari, he's a really mature guy," Sarkisian said. "He kind of reminds me of a of a younger Graceson Littleton that way with the mindset, football is important to him. He works at his craft. He's humble enough to know what he doesn't know, and he's willing to be coached. He has a physical presence about him." away.headline: 5 Texas starters listed as questionable ahead of contest against Mizzou football
away.blurb: Missouri football's injury report was unchanged from last week on the SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report with Malae Fonoti, Josh Atkins and Gavin Hoffman all listed as out. The Tigers' opponent, the Texas Longhorns, had a much more extensive list that included five starters listed as questionable. Star edge rusher Colin Simmons headlines the list of questionable Longhorns after missing the last two games. Despite not playing since Oct. 17, Simmons leads the country with 10.5 sacks. Running back Hollywood Smothers and tight end Nick Townsend were listed as out after playing last week against Mississippi State. Smothers, who suffered an injury against the Bulldogs, is second in rushing yards on the Longhorns, leaving the bulk of carries to Raleek Brown. Townsend, who has been dealing with an ongoing injury, has started three games this season and recorded two catches and four yards last week. Of the remaining Longhorns, Trevor Goosby is out for the season and Richard Wesley has been out since Oct. 17. The Tigers (6-2, 3-2 Southeastern Conference) are looking to become the first ranked team to defeat No. 7 Texas (6-2, 3-2) this season, after the Longhorns have gone 3-0 against ranked opponents. If Missouri comes out on top, it would be its second top-10 victory of the season. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/missouri as 5 Texas starters listed as questionable ahead of contest against Mizzou football . The other two most notable names on the injury report are the Longhorns' top receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman. Wingo has appeared in every game up to this point and leads the Longhorns in receptions (36) and receiving yards (470) and has added a team-second four receiving touchdowns. Coleman has appeared in every contest as well, is third in receiving yards (409) and leads the team with seven receiving touchdowns. In the secondary, the Longhorns could be without two big names in starting defensive backs Kade Phillips and Graceson Littleton. Phillips has started in all eight games and Littleton has started in seven contests. Phillips ranks fifth in the team in tackles (34) and is tied for third in pass breakups with four, while Littleton has logged 28 tackles and ranks second with five pass breakups. On the Tigers end, the three players listed last week were the same on Wednesday's report, signaling that Ahmad Hardy will be making his home debut Saturday. Multiple players were upgraded to probable, but the bad news is that the status of two others remained unchanged. UPGRADED TO PROBABLE: CB Kade Phillips, WR Ryan Wingo, CB Graceson Littleton REMAINS QUESTIONABLE: DE Colin Simmons, WR Cam Coleman RULED OUT: RB Hollywood Smothers, OL Trevor Goosby, TE Nick Townsend, DE Richard Wesley According to ESPN's Pete Thamel, Simmons traveled with the team to Columbia and will test out his ankle injury during pregame warmups. If he plays, Simmons is expected to be on a pitch count. It truly looks like he will be a game-time decision. Simmons has missed the past two games and the expectation was that he could return against Missouri but that remains to be seen. The Longhorns will continue to lean on Wingo and Mosley moving forward if Coleman is officially ruled out against Mizzou and beyond. So far this season, Coleman has tallied 23 catches for 409 yards and seven touchdowns. 5 Texas Starters Questionable on Initial Injury Report vs. Missouri The Texas Longhorns are dealing with some major injury questions before visiting Missouri in Columbia on Saturday. Coleman suffered an upper-body injury in the first half during the win over Mississippi State. He returned to the sideline with a sling on his left arm/shoulder. Per Thamel's report, there is not a ton of optimism that Coleman will play against Missouri. Though Coleman is arguably Texas' most talented receiver, the production hasn't quite matched that. He's the team's third-leading receiver behind Wingo and Emmett Mosley despite playing in all eight games this season. Steve Sarkisian Confident If Other Players Need to Step Up If Littleton or Phillips are unable to play, freshman cornerback Samari Matthews would be one of the players expected to step up. Should that happen, Sarkisian is confident in what he brings to the table. "Samari, he's a really mature guy," Sarkisian said. "He kind of reminds me of a of a younger Graceson Littleton that way with the mindset, football is important to him. He works at his craft. He's humble enough to know what he doesn't know, and he's willing to be coached. He has a physical presence about him." home.headline: Texas's final injury report provides a slight reprieve for the Longhorns vs. Missouri
home.blurb: With one brutal injury list after another, it looked like the Horns could be without as many as eight or nine starters. Luckily, in Texas's final availability report ahead of kickoff, it looked like the Horns might actually catch a break as a few players shifted toward being available. On Friday night, defensive backs Kade Phillips and Graceson Littleton were both listed as "probable" after spending a majority of the week under the "questionable" category, as was wide receiver Ryan Wingo. However, as most injury reports go, it was not all good news for Texas. We have known for a couple of weeks that starting left tackle Trevor Goosby was out for the rest of the season, but starting running back Hollywood Smothers joined him on that list after tearing his MCL. Additionally, edge rusher Richard Wesley and tight end Nick Townsend were both on the availability report, once again, as "out." Then, star edge rusher Colin Simmons was listed as "questionable" for a third straight week after suffering a high-ankle sprain against the Florida Gators in Week 7. Wide receiver Cam Coleman joined Simmons in the grey area after getting beat up against Mississippi State last week. On ESPN's College GameDay , Pete Thamel reported that the two were "game-time decisions," with Simmons seeing a larger likelihood of suiting up and actually setting foot on the field. OUT: Trevor Goosby (OL), Hollywood Smothers (RB), Nick Townsend (TE), Richard Wesley (EDGE) QUESTIONABLE: Colin Simmons (EDGE), Cam Coleman (WR) PROBABLE: Ryan Wingo (WR), Kade Phillips (DB), Graceson Littleton (DB) While any injuries are far from ideal, the final availability report of the week was far from the worst news for the Longhorns. Yes, a few stars are still out or doubtful, but it also looked like quite a few would be available in the top-20 SEC matchup. OUT: Malae Fonoti (RB), Josh Atkins (OL), Gavin Hoffman (TE) Last week saw the return of Missouri's star running back Ahmad Hardy, who had suffered a gunshot wound to the leg this offseason. While he did not see many reps in Week 9, one could expect his workload to increase as the Tigers and the Longhorns clashed. No. 7 Texas and No. 18 Missouri are scheduled to kick off at 11 a.m. CT on Saturday, Nov. 7, and the game will be available on both ABC and fuboTV. With a win, the Horns could take one more step toward cementing their place in this season's College Football Playoff. home.headline: Missouri football injury updates on official SEC report Wednesday before Texas
home.blurb: Mizzou published its first of four SEC-mandated availability and injury reports on Wednesday, Nov. 4, ahead of its game this coming Saturday against Texas, and added no new names to begin the week. That marks the second straight week that the Tigers have opened a game week without any injury concerns beyond players previously ruled out for the year. The major injury news comes out of Austin, Texas, as the Longhorns listed multiple starters and key players with availability designations. On offense for Texas, starting wideouts Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo were listed as questionable, and rotational running back Hollywood Smothers has been ruled out. On defense for the Longhorns, star defensive end Colin Simmons is questionable. Starting nickel Graceson Littleton and cornerback Kade Phillips, who have played the fifth- and sixth-most defensive snaps for the Longhorns this season, respectively, also were questionable. As it has since SEC play started, Mizzou ruled out running back Malae Fonoti, who is out for the season, right tackle Josh Atkins, who Eli Drinkwitz said he does not expect to be available this year, and tight end Gavin Hoffman. EDG #1 Colin Simmons (Questionable) WR #1 Ryan Wingo (Questionable) WR #8 Cam Coleman (Questionable) DB #8 Kade Phillips (Questionable) DB #29 Graceson Littleton (Questionable) The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. The reports are not technically injury reports, which some teams — Mizzou often included — provided in years prior. Instead, they are lists that include any players ruled unavailable or possibly unavailable for upcoming games. That could be for any number of reasons, including but not limited to injuries. home.headline: Texas Gets Devastating Hollywood Smothers Injury Update Ahead of Missouri
home.blurb: Texas RB Hollywood Smothers Out for Rest of Season Texas Gets Devastating Hollywood Smothers Injury Update Ahead of Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Story by Texas Longhorns On SI videos Texas Gets Devastating Hollywood Smothers Injury Update Ahead of Missouri Texas Longhorns running back Hollywood Smothers (2) warms up before a game against the Mississippi State Cougars at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Zach Dimmitt · Texas Longhorns On SI videos Thu, November 5, 2026 at 8:01 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Texas Longhorns have been no stranger to the injury bug this season, though this hasn't stopped the team from being firmly in the College Football Playoff race. Already without starting left tackle Trevor Goosby for the remainder of the season, the injury issues have piled up for Texas headed into Saturday's road matchup with the Missouri Tigers. Now, the Longhorns are receiving worst-case scenario news when it comes to starting running back Hollywood Smothers, who exited last week's game against Mississippi State with an apparent lower-body injury. Smothers will miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to a torn MCL in his knee, according to multiple reports. He started the year off as the team's starter after transferring in from NC State. In the second half against Mississippi State, Smothers took a hard hit to his lower body and sat on the turf holding his left knee. He was then helped off the field by trainers and was unable to put any weight on his left leg. Smothers finishes his 2026 season with 69 carries for 283 yards and two touchdowns along with 10 catches for 79 yards and another score. His pair of rushing touchdowns came in one of the biggest moments of Texas' season, as he had two scores in the fourth quarter against Ohio State, highlighted by the game-winning touchdown in the final minute to complete the comeback. The Longhorns have already gotten accustomed to life without Smothers this season. He previously dealt with ankle and shoulder injuries, forcing him to miss games against Tennessee and Ole Miss. Texas running back Raleek Brown now becomes the no-doubt starter moving forward for the Longhorns. So far this season, he's tallied 92 carries for 452 yards and five touchdowns along with 12 catches for 54 yard and another score. This was highlighted by an impressive performance in the win over Ole Miss when he had 23 carries for 157 yards. Behind him, Michael Terry III and Derrek Cooper will continue to receive an uptick in snaps. Terry has impressed and appears to have overtaken Cooper on the depth chart. It feels likely Terry will be Brown's backup moving forward. home.blurb: Wednesday's SEC player availability report confirmed that the No. 7 Texas Longhorns will be undermanned for Saturday's crucial road tilt against the No. 18 Missouri Tigers in Columbia with two new players ruled out and five starters listed as questionable. The injury situation for the Tigers looks much different with the return of star running back Ahmad Hardy with only three players listed on the availability report, all ruled out. Kickoff is set for 12 p.m. ET on FOX. Despite what I expect to be a hostile environment at Minnesota's Huntington Bank Stadium, the Bruins enter Saturday's Big Ten clash as 5.5-point road favorites, with a moneyline of -192. The over/under sits at 39.5 total points. Here's my UCLA vs. Minnesota prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 7. UCLA vs Minnesota Odds, Betting Line, Point Spread UCLA vs Minnesota Spread : UCLA -3.5, Minnesota +3.5 UCLA vs Minnesota Over/Under : 38.5 Total Points UCLA vs Minnesota Moneyline : UCLA ML -182, Minnesota ML +152 UCLA has been the biggest surprise of the college football season, as first-year head coach Bob Chesney has ripped through a relatively difficult conference schedule and is now one of just three undefeated teams at 8-0. This has all happened despite losing quarterback Nico Iamaleava to a season-ending injury against Oregon , I think the loss of the former Vol made this Bruins bunch even better, thanks to the spectacular play of backup Ty Dieffenbach . While many initially saw Iamaleava's injury as a major roadblock to their playoff quest, the signal-caller had been extremely turnover-prone and objectively overrated nationally. Nico had thrown just four passing touchdowns all year before getting hurt and turned the ball over six times during that stretch. In his absence, Dieffenbach has thrown for 683 passing yards while turning the ball over only once — a vital attribute for a squad that relies heavily on its defense. Running back Wayne Knight has also been spectacular for Chesney's rushing attack, racking up 680 yards on the ground at an impressive 6.2 yards per carry. Knight's 12 rushing touchdowns rank seventh nationally, and I expect him to play a major role in what should be a difficult road atmosphere. Knight is one of several key players Chesney brought to UCLA from James Madison, and he leads a versatile backfield that also features Anthony Woods and Jaivian Thomas. The Bruins are battle-tested and continue to impress each week, and this matchup against Minnesota will undoubtedly be a difficult challenge if UCLA is to advance to 9-0. This Big Ten showdown will have major playoff implications for the Bruins as the regular season comes to a close. The season has been up and down for the Golden Gophers , who enter their Week 10 matchup with a 5-3 record. Minnesota has looked inconsistent in head coach PJ Fleck's 10th season at the helm, losing two of its last three contests after an impressive 4-1 start. Junior quarterback Drake Lindsey has looked impressive in his second season under center, throwing for 1,592 yards through the air over the first eight games. Running back TJ Thomas leads the rushing attack with 379 yards and is the feature tailback in a backfield that also features Darius Taylor and Xavier Ford . The Gophers have been far more efficient through the air, though, with a receiving corps that includes senior wideout Noah Jennings and speedster slot option Javon Tracy, who have combined for 855 receiving yards. This will be a huge test for defensive coordinator Danny Collins' unit, which has looked very impressive over the first nine weeks, with opponents scoring just 20.5 PPG on average, ranking 35th in the FBS. Collins' aggressive, heavy-blitzing 4-3 base schematics will be tested against an extremely well-balanced UCLA offense that rarely turns the ball over. While this clash is undoubtedly more significant for UCLA, it still matters for a Gopher bunch looking to finish on a strong note before bowl season. While UCLA has looked spectacular in its first year under Chesney, I expect Saturday to be very difficult for the Bruins, who will be under pressure in front of a rowdy Gopher fanbase. UCLA boasts one of the premier defenses in college football, ranking seventh in opponent yards per game, 13th in opponent passing yards per game and 10th in opponent rushing yards per game. Fleck's defense is also extremely dominant, ranking inside the top 25 in several defensive metrics. In a game where I expect UCLA to start sluggish on the road, with an earlier start time than the Bruins are accustomed to, I favor backing under 7.5 points in the first quarter at -135 in what I expect to be a low-scoring defensive battle. Pick: 1Q Under 7.5 (-136 · FanDuel )

The Bruins were No. 8 in the first round of College Football Playoff rankings, which doesn't matter. If they end up 10-2, as a Big Ten team, they're a mortal lock to get into the CFP. But at this point, they want a spot in the Big Ten Championship, and they're good enough to beat anyone left on the slate. Minnesota has proven it's almost good enough to beat anyone, losing a brutal 23-16 heartbreaker to Indiana last week. It beat Iowa and Michigan, but a weird 41-13 loss at Purdue is an issue for an at-large CFP spot. However, win out, and there's a shot at getting into the Big Ten title game. UCLA vs Minnesota: Quick Hits UCLA gets Illinois in the Rose Bowl next, then has to travel to Michigan, and finishes up down the road at USC. Minnesota goes to Penn State next week, hosts Northwestern, and close with the Paul Bunyan Axe game at Wisconsin. The two programs have only faced each other four times, with Minnesota winning the last meeting 21-17 in 2024. The Gophers are 3-1, starting with a 21-3 win in the 19162 Rose Bowl. How To Watch UCLA vs Minnesota Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis, MN – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why UCLA Will Win Run, run, and keep running. There's no real mystery to what UCLA does. It blasts away, with the ground game, gets just enough from the passing game to get by, and then it relies on the defense to take care of everything else. It starts with third down stops. Only Nebraska – at least before the loss to Illinois – is better at defensively on third downs than the Bruins. That allows UCLA to dominate the time of possession battle, the rested defense forces a ton of takeaways, the offense capitalizes … repeat. However … Why Minnesota Will Win UCLA runs well, Minnesota doesn't. Minnesota can throw well, UCLA doesn't. Other than that, these two do almost all of the same things. You want third down defense? Minnesota is sixth in the nation, allowing teams to convert just 28% of their chances. Time of possession? The Gophers aren't as good as UCLA, but they're fine, usually keeping the ball for close to 32 minutes per game. And then there are the takeaways – Minnesota is good at that, too. UCLA vs Minnesota Prediction, Betting Lines The whole Big Noon Kickoff aspect to this is a problem for UCLA. The Bruins have to be ready to rumble at 9:00 am Los Angeles time. And then there's the other issue. When the ball gets kicked off in Minneapolis, it will be around 71 degrees in LA. The temperature should hover around 40 degrees and feel more like 32ish for the entire game in Huntington Bank. UCLA will be pushed and tested, and Minnesota will take advantage of that early, but the score will be kept low throughout, and the Bruins will still be alive in the second half, when the ground game starts to take over. It'll be another tremendously entertaining Minnesota game to kick off a whale of a Saturday. Signing Roman Voss in the 2026 high school cycle was one of P.J. Fleck’s biggest recruiting wins of his Gophers tenure. We’re quickly learning why Alabama and numerous top programs were after Voss, as Minnesota’s true freshman tight end continues to find his footing this season. Now 6-foot-4 and 235 pounds, Voss was a decorated prep athlete at Jackson County Central (JCC) High School in southern Minnesota. The Huskies played at the Class 2A level, but Voss was so dominant he won Minnesota Gatorade Player of the Year and Minnesota Mr. Football as a senior. He played quarterback and finished his senior season with 1,902 yards and 21 touchdowns through the air and 1,893 yards and 30 more touchdowns on the ground. Voss’s final college choice came down to Alabama and Minnesota. He also had notable offers from programs like Miami (FL), USC, Oklahoma, Auburn and more. He was dubbed a four-star prospect and the second-best player in Minnesota, according to the 247Sports Composite. Transitioning from quarterback at the high school level to tight end in the Big Ten isn’t easy, so there were plenty of questions about how quickly Voss could contribute for the Gophers. Through seven weeks, he has seven receptions for 117 yards and two touchdowns, all of which are the most by a tight end on Minnesota’s roster. Voss has still played only 94 offensive snaps this season, but when he’s on the field, the Gophers want to get him the ball. He has run a route on 95.5 percent of those snaps, which emphasizes that Minnesota sees him as more of an offensive weapon than a blocker at this moment. That leaves Voss, Oklahoma transfer Kaden Helms, third-year player Jacob Simpson and fellow true freshman George Rohl as the Gophers’ only healthy tight ends who have played significant snaps this season. Minnesota’s offense has averaged just 14.5 points per game since the bye week. Voss has averaged 36.5 yards in the same span, which is just one yard per game fewer than Darius Taylor, who received 18 more touches. Javon Tracy’s 53.5 yards per game is the only mark significantly higher than Voss’s, but he has also gotten significantly more opportunities. Voss has more yards than TJ Thomas, Noah Jennings and Jalen Smith over the last two games. If Johnson and Walsh end up missing this week’s game against UCLA, Minnesota’s game plan should include getting Voss more involved. It’s time to take off the training wheels. Nothing appears to be working consistently right now, and getting the football into the hands of your best playmakers is typically a sound strategy to fix that. picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for LSU against Alabama
picks.blurb: LSU's Tiger Stadium will host another major SEC rival matchup of the season as the Crimson Tide pays a visit to Baton Rouge for a Week 10 showdown. Both teams are heading into the high-stakes matchup after a rested bye week as both teams work on their list of player injuries. The game's outcome could decide both teams' fates in the playoffs, creating an anticipated matchup in the long-standing rivalry. Here are three bold predictions for LSU's matchup against Alabama. Trey'Dez Green Will Be Alabama's Biggest Target LSU is able to recover from some of its injuries, including tight end Trey'Dez Green , who returns after missing four of the team's mid-season games. Green appeared in the team's defeat over Auburn, putting up 50 receiving yards across five receptions and a touchdown. Green ended up leaving the game early, after head coach Lane Kiffin reported that Auburn's defense was attempting hip drop tackles on the talented tight end, a move that significantly increases a player's chances of getting injured and one that was banned in the NFL in 2024. While he may not be getting targeted in the same way against Alabama, he still will have all the pressure on him, making him a risky target for Leavitt, who's already struggled with turnovers this season. The 6'7, 237 lb. tight end is the ultimate weapon on offense, one that Alabama has experience in facing, being aware of his ability to contribute to the Tigers' offensive success and making all the moves to limit it on Saturday. LSU's Defense Will Hold Keelon Russell To 170 Passing Yards LSU's defensive unit, one of the best groups in the league, will face a major challenge against Alabama's offense, led by quarterback Keelon Russell . Russell is also anticipating the obstacle of the Bayou Bandits, a team that has allowed 172.8 passing yards from opponents per game. Limiting Russell to the magic number of 170 passing yards will prove its ability to hit Alabama where it hurts, putting pressure on its offensive leader. During the team's back-to-back losses this season against Georgia and Tennessee, Russell put up a season low of 147 passing yards during the trip to Neyland Stadium, scoring the only touchdown for the Tide during the game. Against the Bulldogs, Russell still couldn't hit the 200 mark, ending the loss with 185 passing yards. Now that he will face one of the league's most dangerous defenses, a unit that once held the most sacks this season, Russell's passing production could take another major blow if the defense can keep up the pressure all game long. LSU Will Record 5+ Sacks LSU's defense can limit Russell's production from the first snap, closing in on him in the pocket and recording more than five sacks against the Tide quarterback. He sits in the Top-10 for the quarterback with the most sacks this season, recording a staggering 22 so far. Against LSU's defense - a unit that met the program's record for the most sacks in one game during Week 2 of the season - Russell and his offensive line could be in major trouble. This production will come from the exterior of the line, with defensive end Princewill Umanmielen becoming Russell's biggest nightmare as the leader of the defense with nine sacks so far. Even if the Crimson Tide can put extra pressure on Umanmielen's side, defensive end Jordan Ross brings the same threat on the opposite end, as major pressure will be closing in on Russell all game long. Sam Leavitt and Kiffin will try to break the streak in his debut season. LSU is coming off two back-to-back big wins before the bye week. The Tigers crushed Mississippi State 31-0 and Auburn 38-17. Sam Leavitt threw seven touchdowns and ran for another in that two-game span, plus Jackson Harris caught four of those touchdowns and totaled 263 receiving yards. LSU's defense has only allowed 281 yards through the air in those two games as well, so nothing should come easy in Death Valley for one of the best home defenses in the country. LSU and Alabama would love to notch a signature win. Alabama's opportunistic secondary could trouble Sam Leavitt and the offense. If Leavitt protects the ball and the defensive line takes advantage of a potentially vulnerable Crimson Tide offensive line, LSU should win. Tiger Stadium will be deafening, and I think the Tigers will make a statement on Saturday. LSU 35, Alabama 24 I think that the Tigers win a close one at home. This freshly healthy Alabama squad will be a tough challenge for these LSU Tigers, but I think that the LSU defense will come up with a pick-six late in the game to seal their victory. LSU 31, Alabama 28 LSU and Lane Kiffin are ready to take down Alabama. For Kiffin, he's 0-5. For LSU, a three-year losing streak will end.
