The Tigers' defense is ready for the challenge too. With Alabama missing some key pieces on the o-line, and LSU's dominant pass rush, the matchup easily favors the Tigers. LSU 45, Alabama 21 Brooke Benedict LSU and Alabama have shown a similar weakness this season, as both teams reveal critical system errors and momentum failures when trailing in a game. Alabama showed this against Tennessee and LSU has shown this against Ole Miss, both major opponents this season. As Saturday's matchup brings the same level of competition, it's key that both teams don't let the score turn lopsided. With the home-field advantage, I think LSU will be able to gain the momentum early, and Alabama will lose key momentum in the environment of Tiger Stadium. LSU 28, Alabama 20 While LSU vs. Alabama isn't a "storied" rivalry, it's perhaps some of the best football that gets played each year, and this matchup will be no different. Kiffin is looking for his first signature win with LSU, and if Sam Leavitt continues to play the same way he has the last two weeks, I expect it to happen. I also think that our defense is a lot stronger than theirs is; we are holding opponents to fewer points per game than their team is, despite both defenses being really good. In terms of our offense, I think that Sam Levitt has been on the up and up the past couple of games; he hasn't thrown any interceptions, and he's looking more like the 2024 CFP quarterback that he once was. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling. The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. Ohio State vs. Oregon: Need to know Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana , it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore ). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road. Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. There are a total of seven top-25 matchups coming, and with the new College Football Rankings now released, the stakes have gone up. Among those ranked matchups is a Big Ten showdown between the No. 23 Oregon Ducks and No. 12 Ohio State Buckeyes . We've seen these two partake in some monumental games over the years, whether it was the 2010 Rose Bowl or the 2014 National Championship Game, as well as more recent meetings as conference foes, like the 2024 Rose Bowl, or a regular-season win for the Ducks earlier that year. While neither team has quite had the success this year that they forecasted before the year started, this is still expected to be a monumental matchup, with the season riding on the line for both schools. All week, we've broken down the game and analyzed what we expect to happen, but now let's take a look at what the national media guys think. Here's a look at what some of the biggest names in the sport are saying about Oregon's matchup against Ohio State on Saturday afternoon: Pick: 30-20, Ohio State Analysis: "I'm going to say Ohio State wins this game at home. They have to. They win 30-20 to cover the 7.5. I'm worried about Raiola with some pressure on him in that game." Dan Rubenstein Pick: Ohio State by a TD Analysis: "I can't, in good conscience, take Oregon in this spot. I think they are making strides. I think they're getting better, but I think you're talking about Luke Fahey messing up and not being ready for this moment and buckling under pressure once again a little bit, which is understandable. I think Ohio State's able to do enough to win this game. Maybe ugly, maybe in like a 17-13 way. Maybe Oregon's able to push around the Ohio State offensive line and get a strip sack here, and you know, get some easy points. But I don't know. I think this game simulated 100 times, Ohio State probably wins it 73 times, so I'm going Ohio State to win this game right now." Ty Hildenbrandt Pick: 20-17, Oregon Analysis: "I think it's something like 20-17. Okay, I think it's close. I'm going to pick Oregon. I'm going to continue the trend of not worrying about who the road team is, which will be to my detriment, I'm sure. Oregon's got a really good red zone defense." Pick: 25-18, Ohio State Analysis: "I think Ohio State wins. I'm not touching the spread. I would say Oregon covers based on our final score, but I don't want to touch it. Final score: Ohio State gets back on the right side of things, 25-18. The Buckeyes over the Ducks in Columbus." Greg McCelroy Pick: 24-20, Ohio State Analysis: "I'm taking Ohio State to win the game, 24-20. Oregon covers the number. I also think the under is the right play as well. And Oregon's going to have a cleaner pocket. Ohio State will have the best player on the field. And in Columbus in November, the best player on the field I think is going to get the last word." Davison was listed as out on the Ducks' availability report released Nov. 4 by the Big Ten Conference. McClellan, who was listed as probable on Wednesday's availability report, broke his foot during pregame warmups prior to the Portland State game on Sept. 18 and has missed the last six games. Before getting hurt, he had seven catches for 170 yards and one TD in two games. Also out for a third-straight game is receiver Messiah Hampton, who was arrested a week ago for eluding police and reckless driving. Tony Cumberland – The four-star freshman defensive tackle from Eugene's Willamette High School was injured in an offseason car accident and remains out. "It's a work in progress with him," Oregon defensive line coach Tony Tuioti said Aug. 17. "I don't think it's going to be anything that we'll be able to see him soon. But he's made so much progress. I think the thing that's most important is that we have him with us and just having him in the room brings a smile to all our faces." Trent Ferguson – The junior left guard is out for the season with a knee injury suffered against Oklahoma State Sept. 12 during his first career start. Aaron Flowers – The starting safety is out for "the foreseeable future" after having surgery on his shoulder, Lanning said Oct. 14. He left the game against USC on Sept. 26 and hasn't played since. Brayden Platt – Lanning announced after the first week of fall camp that the junior inside linebacker was going to miss time with an undisclosed injury and wouldn't put a timetable on his return. Jeremiah McClellan – The starting wide receiver was listed as probable for the Ohio State game. He broke his foot during pregame warmups against Portland State Sept. 18 and has missed six games. In the long history of this rivalry, there's a good case that this is the biggest game ever. In his first year on the job, Will Stein has led Kentucky to a 7-1 start and a great shot at reaching the College Football Playoff with just four games remaining. His major transfer portal additions -- particularly quarterback Kenny Minchey and the offensive line -- clicked almost immediately. To this point, the Wildcats have passed all but one test they've faced, but the level of difficulty rises this weekend. Kentucky must continue to play clean football if it wants to come away with a win in Knoxville. Tennessee had two weeks to wallow in the "what if" after its three-point loss to South Carolina , but the team has to get back in the saddle this weekend. The Volunteers have the chance to pick up their second top-10 win of the season, which would really boost their CFP rankings. There's no doubt that the Vols have a playoff-caliber defense and running game, but can Josh Heupel fix the passing attack? Tennessee must improve there to reach its ceiling. Here is everything you need to know about this top-15 rivalry matchup in Knoxville. Tennessee vs. Kentucky: Need to know Rare ranked matchup: These teams have met well over 100 times, but this is just the fourth ranked matchup in history. Most recently, Tennessee and Kentucky played a top-25 matchup in 2022, with the Volunteers winning in a blowout. Prior to that, the only times the Vols and Wildcats were ranked simultaneously were in 1950 and 1951. That means there's a very good case for this matchup to be the biggest in the history of this rivalry. Games with stakes in this series usually go the way of Tennessee, but can Stein turn the tables on Saturday night? Kentucky not in the giving spirit: The holidays are approaching quickly, but Kentucky has not been feeling very generous. One of the driving factors behind the Wildcats' success is their incredible plus-13 turnover margin. That ranks first in the SEC and fourth in the entire country. For the first time since 2013, Kentucky has avoided turning the ball over in three consecutive games. If any team can end that streak, it's probably Tennessee, which has a great defense and has forced 14 turnovers in eight games. The Vols just have to protect the ball on offense. Heavy dose of DeSean Bishop : Kentucky defensive coordinator Jay Bateman probably doesn't need my advice, but I would suggest he lock in on Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop. He's been the engine of the Vols offense, and his 957 rushing yards rank sixth in the country. His 12 rushing touchdowns are tied for ninth. Over the last four games, Bishop has averaged 29 carries and 159 yards. If the Wildcats can contain Bishop and force Tennessee to throw the ball, that could be a recipe for success, but only one team has effectively shut Bishop down to this point. Defensively, the Wildcats have thrived on timely turnovers to mask their 118th-ranked third-down defense and a secondary ranked 94th in passing success rate. DeSean Bishop and Daune Morris will be called upon early and often to punish UK's thin linebacker depth as the Volunteers pull away late against a fatigued defense behind sustained long drives. I also expect both teams to struggle in obvious passing situations, as both offensive lines rank in the Bottom 25% in sack rate allowed. But Tennessee's grinding offense, combined with the success I expect its defense to have, will keep this south of 50 points — a number only one of their SEC games has reached. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Tennessee game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Kentucky vs. Tennessee game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction chrisbeasmore · SB Nation Tue, November 3, 2026 at 2:23 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky Football moved up one spot to No. 8 in the AP Top 25 Poll despite not playing a game this past weekend. One major reason for the Wildcats' rise was Ohio State's loss to USC on Saturday. Kentucky is now 7-1 overall and 5-1 in SEC play, making the Wildcats one of the most surprising teams in college football this season, especially under first-year head coach Will Stein. The last time Kentucky took the field, the Wildcats defeated Vanderbilt 34-17 at home. However, they got off to a slow start, falling behind 10-0 before turning things around and taking the lead into halftime. Kentucky eventually took care of business to secure another SEC victory. Now, the Wildcats will hit the road to Knoxville this weekend to face the Tennessee Volunteers. Kentucky's most recent road game came against Oklahoma, where the Wildcats escaped Norman with a 21-13 victory. Kentucky will look to replicate that performance against Tennessee, but the Volunteers' defense has been one of the nation's best and will present a significant challenge. Tennessee Volunteers (6-2, 3-2) Tennessee has an impressive defense, but the Volunteers also have a talented running back in DeSean Bishop. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow him down, as he can make opposing defenses pay if he gets into a rhythm. Meanwhile, Tennessee's quarterback situation has been a concern, with the Volunteers relying on George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon. The two quarterbacks have different styles. MacIntyre tends to be more conservative, often targeting receivers near or behind the line of scrimmage, while Brandon is more willing to push the ball downfield. It will be interesting to see which quarterback Tennessee turns to on Saturday against Kentucky. At wide receiver, Mike Matthews has emerged as the Volunteers' primary target, leading the team in receptions and receiving yards. Defensively, Tennessee has been impressive, recording 35 sacks, eight interceptions, and nine fumble recoveries this season. Kentucky will need to protect the football and avoid costly mistakes to have a chance to leave Knoxville with a victory. The Wildcats will likely need a near-perfect performance on both sides of the ball. Turnovers could quickly swing the momentum in Tennessee's favor, especially with the Volunteers playing in front of their home crowd at Neyland Stadium. Tennessee had an impressive 26-10 victory over Alabama at home. However, the Volunteers have also suffered a couple of notable losses, including a 20-17 defeat to Texas at home and most recently a heartbreaking 27-24 loss to South Carolina on a game-winning field goal. With both teams coming off a bye week, Kentucky will have an opportunity to prepare for Tennessee's defensive strengths. Still, winning on the road against a talented Volunteers team will be a difficult task. How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Tennessee Volunteers Location: Neyland Stadium — Knoxville, Tennessee Date: Saturday, November 7 Time: 6:15 p.m. ET Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog. ESPN win probability: Kentucky has just a 33.2% chance of winning, according to ESPN . Our early prediction Kentucky enters this matchup at 7-1 overall and 5-1 in SEC play, having won six consecutive games since its home loss to Alabama in the second game of the season. The Wildcats will look to keep that momentum going, improve to 8-1 overall and 6-1 in conference play, and strengthen their case for a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, the challenge does not get any easier this weekend. Kentucky must travel to Knoxville to face a Tennessee team with a dominant defense and plenty of motivation of its own. The Volunteers are also coming off a bye week and will be ready to respond after their loss to South Carolina. While Kentucky has been playing some of its best football of the season, I believe the Wildcats' winning streak comes to an end in a close, low-scoring contest. Tennessee's defense will make things difficult for Kentucky's offense, and the home-field advantage at Neyland Stadium could ultimately prove to be the difference. Final score: Tennessee 27, Kentucky 21. How do you see this one playing out?

picks.headline: Tennessee football vs Kentucky picks: Vols don't lose to Wildcats in Knoxville, right?
picks.blurb: Tennessee football vs Kentucky picks: Vols don't lose to Wildcats in Knoxville, right? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Knoxville News Sentinel · The Tennessean Sat, November 7, 2026 at 10:06 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Tennessee football opens a November to either remember or forget with a top-15 matchup against Kentucky on Nov. 7 at Neyland Stadium The Vols (6-2, 3-2 SEC) lost at South Carolina two weeks ago on a last-second field goal, earning a second SEC loss before the final month of the season. Kentucky (7-1, 5-1) is also coming off of an open date and has a clear path to the SEC Championship Game and the CFP. First-year coach Will Stein has molded his roster into a team that limits its mistakes and maximizes other teams' turnovers. UK has beaten Tennessee in Knoxville once since 1984, the 2020 win in front of a COVID-limited crowd at Neyland. Here are Knox News' staff predictions for Tennessee-Kentucky: Tennessee-Kentucky expert predictions Adam Sparks, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 28, Kentucky 24 The Vols can certainly beat themselves against the most disciplined team in the SEC. Kentucky leads the league in turnover margin and fewest penalties. But UT can take control of this game by winning the line of scrimmage. That means DeSean Bishop earns bruising yards and UT's defensive line collapses the pocket around Kenny Minchey. Give Tennessee the edge because of the overwhelming atmosphere of Neyland Stadium in a night game in dark mode. Emmett Siegel, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 24, Kentucky 20 The Vols still have to find something in their passing game , which is statistically the worst in the SEC. Even if that doesn't come to fruition, though, Tennessee's rushing attack and defense have been good enough to beat the toughest teams on its schedule. Perhaps the open week helped Tennessee clean up some of last game's mistakes before playing a team that doesn't make many. Playing at home could push it over the top. Cora Hall, UT beat reporter: Kentucky 27, Tennessee 24 Both teams are had a week off and are rested going into this matchup, and the Wildcats have proven they can will their way to a win when it matters. The Vols will get close, but they've been too inconsistent to bet on a win here. Stephen Thompson, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 17, Kentucky 13 I've surrendered to the idea that George MacIntyre is who he is, at least for now. But Tennessee's defense is as good as any in the country and the Neyland effect will be a difference maker in another ugly, but tight win for the Vols. Wynton Jackson, sports reporter: Tennessee 26, Kentucky 21 The Vols likely need to be perfect throughout the rest of the season to reach the College Football Playoff. Coming off the bye, that road starts with an unexpected matchup against No. 7 Kentucky. The Wildcats have solid wins, but a trip to Neyland with a national spotlight brings heightened pressure. John Adams, columnist: Tennessee 27, Kentucky 20 The Wildcats have a better record and a higher national ranking than the Vols. Moreover, Kentucky is clearly headed in the right direction under first-year coach Will Stein. But history tells us that Tennessee is always the wrong direction for Kentucky football, which has lost 38 of the previous 41 games in the series. Gentry Estes, Tennessean columnist: Tennessee 23, Kentucky 14 Props to the Wildcats on a great season, but it just feels like they are due for a letdown in a tough rivalry road game. Neyland should be jumping for this one. This article originally appeared on Knoxville News Sentinel: Tennessee football vs Kentucky picks: Vols don't lose to Wildcats in Knoxville, right?

picks.headline: Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction
picks.blurb: Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to a hostile Neyland Stadium to take on the Tennessee Volunteers at 6:15 P.M. ET on Saturday night. This is a massive game with a lot at stake for both teams, the Wildcats are undefeated on the road this season and they will try to continue that streak in this game. We laid out the path to victory for Kentucky and the key areas they need to win to improve to 8-1 on the season. It is time to give some final thoughts on the matchup and give a game prediction. As I stated earlier in the week on my Tennessee defense preview , but I truly think this game comes down to Will Stein's offense versus Jim Knowles' defense. They have met three times and Coach Stein has gotten the best of Knowles in two of those three meetings. Kentucky has to continue to play efficient on offense and play clean. I think they have a great opportunity to methodically move the football down the field as they have all season against this defense. This game starts and ends in the trenches, on both sides of the football. Tennessee's defensive line is the strength of their team, but Kentucky's offensive line is playing better than any offensive line in the country. They have to stabilize defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam, who has been wrecking offensive gameplans all season long. A key matchup to watch is Kentucky center Coleton Price against Gilliam, Price has been one of the best centers in the country and he will have his hands full in this game. Kentucky has to win this game on the line of scrimmage, and I have confidence in the Wildcats offensive line to gain the edge in that matchup. Tennessee's offensive line has been above average as run blockers, but they do struggle in pass protection. Kentucky forcing Tennessee into a dropback heavy game script could be critical, but they have to stop the run in order to do that. Kentucky's defensive line has gotten consistent pressure all season, and I am very intrigued to see how this defensive line gets after a pocket passer like George MacIntyre because they have faced a mobile quarterback in every game this season. Kentucky has to win the line of scrimmage, and this is the best offensive line the Vols have faced this season. I think the Wildcats defensive line has been underrated this year, and they can make a statement on Saturday. The run defense has improved tremendously in the month of October, and slowing down the Vols heavy rushing attack is crucial. If they can force Tennessee into a heavy dropback game, Kentucky will be able to create turnovers like they have all season. Truthfully, I believe the biggest advantage is Kentucky's coaching staff getting two weeks to prepare for this football game. Tennessee is coming off the bye week as well, but Josh Heupel and Jim Knowles are going to do what they do. Kentucky's coaching staff has added plenty of wrinkles week-to-week, so I can only imagine what they will have in store with two weeks to prepare. This is an advantage for Kentucky, particularly on the offensive side of the football. We all know this history of this series, it has not been kind to Kentucky. However, this is a different era of college football and Kentucky football. If you remove the history and helmet logos, I think Kentucky has the advantage at quarterback and offensive line as well as a hotshot head coach that has done an unthinkable turnaround in year one for this program. It will be a close game in the fourth quarter, and how could you not trust Will Stein and Kenny Minchey under those circumstances. Prediction: Kentucky 24, Tennessee 20 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction

Tennessee is favored by 5.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -220. Kentucky is a 5.5-point underdog with a moneyline of +184. The total is set at 49.5 points (-110 / -110). Here's my Kentucky vs. Tennessee prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 7, 2026. Kentucky vs. Tennessee Pick: Tennessee ML (-225) My Tennessee vs. Kentucky best bet is on the Volunteers to win outright. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page , and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Kentucky vs Tennessee Odds, Spread, Line Kentucky vs Tennessee point spread : Kentucky +6.5 (-110), Tennessee -6.5 (-110) Kentucky vs Tennessee over/under : 50.5 (-110o / -110u) Kentucky vs Tennessee moneyline : Kentucky +188, Tennessee -225 In one of the bigger surprises of this college football season, the Wildcats have emerged as one of the best teams in the entire country in head coach Will Stein's first year at the helm. Kentucky senior QB Kenny Minchey has been phenomenal in his first season in Lexington after spending three years at Notre Dame and throwing the ball only 30 times there. Minchey has thrown for 1755 yards and 14 touchdowns over the Wildcats' first eight games this season with just one turnover. Freshman WR Kenny Darby has been Minchey's favorite target with over 500 yards and three touchdowns. Stein's rushing attack has been effective too, with senior tailback CJ Baxter rushing for nearly 500 yards and eight touchdowns. The Wildcat offense is averaging just shy of 33 points per game this season, but will get its most difficult test on Saturday against an elite Tennessee pass rush. Kentucky's defense has thrived under defensive coordinator Jay Bateman, who has built an aggressive, havoc -creating unit that has fared well against some elite SEC offenses this season. The Wildcats lead the SEC in interceptions and pass breakups, boasting an elite secondary led by veteran safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell. While its front seven struggled early this season, Kentucky has improved drastically in the trenches over the course of the season. The 8th-ranked Wildcats are in a great spot to potentially qualify for the playoffs, but still must face several difficult conference opponents, starting with the Vols in Week 10. The 16th-ranked Volunteers put their postseason hopes on the line as Josh Heupel's bunch looks to evade a third loss this season that would very likely ruin their playoff resume. After a very promising 6-1 start to the season despite an ongoing QB battle between George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon , Tennessee was defeated on the road at South Carolina this past weekend for the Vols' second loss of the year. Now they face a must-win game, with lingering questions about whether Heupel will stick with MacIntyre under center or return to top-ranked freshman QB Brandon. Regardless, betting markets have made their stance quite clear, with Tennessee currently listed as a near-touchdown favorite despite the Wildcats' breakout 7-1 campaign. While WR Mike Matthews has recorded over 500 receiving yards this season, Tennessee has relied far more on its rushing attack, with tailback DeSean Bishop rushing for 957 yards and 11 touchdowns, ranking sixth and ninth in all of college football, respectively. However, the Vols' defense has thrived all year, particularly at home, where it allows SEC opponents the third-fewest PPG in the conference (16.25). Jim Knowles was brought in as defensive coordinator this past offseason after serving in the same capacity for Penn State , and has significantly improved a unit that fell to 81st in the country in EPA (Expected Points Added) last season. Tennessee's defense boasts an elite linebacker corps ranked in the top 10 nationally, featuring Edwin Spillman, Amare Campbell, Arion Carter, and Jeremiah Telander. While the Vols' defense has carried this team for most of the season, especially at home in Knoxville, their offense will need to show up in this matchup, given how impressive Michey has been at avoiding turnovers. I expect this to be one of the best matchups in an absolutely loaded Week 10 slate. While I have been very impressed with the Wildcats offense and a much-improved defensive unit, I expect the atmosphere to be quite chaotic given how difficult it is for SEC foes to escape Neyland Stadium in Knoxville with an outright victory. The Vols boast an extremely dominant pass rush that should give Kentucky's offensive line fits considering how much that unit has struggled to contain elite edge pressure. That said, I feel betting markets are giving Tennessee a tad too much credit given their fragile situation at QB. In what I expect to be a pretty closely contested matchup, I'm going with the Volunteers moneyline. I got it at -210 earlier this week as soon as the line opened, and while I typically don't lay that much juice on a moneyline, especially considering the volatility of betting college football, I have confidence Tennessee gets the outright win, but laying close to a touchdown versus a red-hot Wildcat bunch is far from ideal. Though Tennessee's moneyline has since crept up to -230, I still don't mind playing the Vols at that number. Pick: Tennessee ML (-225, FanDuel )

Notre Dame has one of the better offensive lines in college football but has its work cut out against this Miami defensive front. The Hurricanes are allowing just 2.4 yards per rush attempt this year, which means Notre Dame likely won't be able to play the same ball possession type game it likes to. That means CJ Carr's moment is now: Miami has a pass defense that has surrendered huge numbers in narrow escapes against both Florida State and North Carolina. Can Carr do enough to win what could very possibly turn into a track meet between the powerhouse programs? Advantage: Notre Dame Special Teams For the Win? So far we're pretty much at a toss-up, and we figure special teams will end up being huge. Notre Dame doesn't have to have a kick return for a touchdown to win this thing, but overall, its numbers in kick return, punt return, kick coverage, and punt coverage give the Irish an advantage statisically. picks.blurb: Rece Davis Predicts Notre Dame Playoff Problem Ahead of Top-5 Miami Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Notre Dame could find itself in the same College Football Playoff predicament that ended its 2025 season if it can’t beat No. 1 Miami on Saturday, according to ESPN College GameDay host Rece Davis. Davis made the case on ESPN’s College GameDay Podcast with co-hosts Pete Thamel and Dan Wetzel, saying the No. 4 Fighting Irish (7-1) would be in “ very much the same situation as a year ago ” with a loss. Rece Davis on Notre Dame’s resume Notre Dame Fighting Irish head coach Marcus Freeman reacts during the first half against the Brigham Young Cougars | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis said that split will shape the debate over the Irish. He expects them to stay in the field unless the Hurricanes blow them out, but he doesn’t see the questions about their resume going away. “I think Notre Dame will still be OK absent getting run out of the stadium, which I cannot conceive of happening,” Davis said. “So it’s going to be a little bit different than last year, but the argument, the discussion, is going to be the same if they don’t win this game.” He added: “When you get down to who did you play and who did you beat, especially the who did you beat portion of who did you play, they won’t have much on the paper.” Why does Notre Dame’s schedule matter? General view as Brigham Young Cougars fans celebrate on the field after the game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. The Irish beat Wisconsin, Rice, Michigan State, Purdue, North Carolina, Stanford and Navy. After Miami, they close with Boston College, SMU and Syracuse, who are a combined 14-10 and unranked. Notre Dame does carry a protection it lacked last year. The College Football Playoff guarantees the Irish a spot if they finish in the top 12 of the final rankings. A loss to Miami would test that cushion, though, because Notre Dame would sit at 7-2 with no win over a ranked opponent and no ranked teams left on its schedule. Miami vs. Notre Dame stakes Miami Hurricanes head coach Mario Cristobal celebrates after defeating the Florida State Seminoles | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last season, Miami and Notre Dame both finished 10-2, and the selection committee used the Hurricanes’ 27-24 win in Week 1 to award them the final at-large spot. The Irish were the first team out and declined a bowl invitation. Last season, Miami and Notre Dame both finished 10-2, and the selection committee used the Hurricanes’ 27-24 win in Week 1 to award them the final at-large spot. The Irish were the first team out and declined a bowl invitation. Notre Dame athletic director Pete Bevacqua said at the time, “ We feel like the playoff was stolen from our student-athletes.” Davis called the rematch “another little delicious subplot” and said Notre Dame’s frustration “wasn’t necessarily just directed at Miami.” Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman made “ leave no doubt ” the program’s mantra for 2026 after the snub. Saturday gives the Irish that chance against an 8-0 Miami team that leads FBS at 47.6 points per game, while Notre Dame’s defense leads FBS at 236.1 yards allowed per game. The committee releases its first College Football Playoff rankings of the season Tuesday at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN, and Miami vs. Notre Dame kicks off Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. Miami, meanwhile, enters as a +5.5 underdog and is +168 on the moneyline to pull off the upset. The over/udner sits at 57.5 total points. Here's my Miami vs. Notre Dame prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 7. Miami vs. Notre Dame Pick: Notre Dame -5.5 or Better · CJ Carr 21+ Completions (-118) · Jaden Greenhouse Over 40.5 Yards My Notre Dame vs. Miami best bet is on the Fighting Irish to cover the spread, quarterback CJ Carr to complete at least 21 passes and wide receiver Jaden Greathouse to record at least 41 receiving yards. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . Miami vs Notre Dame Odds Miami vs Notre Dame point spread : Notre Dame -5.5 (-110 ), Miami +5.5 (-110) Miami vs Notre Dame over/under : 57.5 (-114o / -106u) Miami vs Notre Dame moneyline : Miami +168, Notre Dame -205 There might not be a better offense in college football than the Miami Hurricanes. Heisman-contending quarterback Darian Mensah has been near flawless this season, posting a turnover-worthy play in just two games this season. The former Duke and Tulane signal-caller stands at 25 touchdowns to just a single interception, a thriving ratio thanks to one of the most dangerous weapons in FBS, slot Malachi Toney. The second-year receiver has 83 targets with more than 1,000 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns. However, Toney will have surgery on his ankle and miss this game. The defense is where Miami has seen a struggle under coordinator Corey Hetherman. The Canes rank 132nd in tackle grading, per PFF , and an uncharacteristic 96th in generating Havoc. The defensive line grades out as one of the best in creating a pass rush, but the back of the 4-2-5 has presented issues in pass coverage. Miami ranks 111th in coverage grading and 105th in passing down Success Rate allowed . Although the Hurricanes are undefeated, covering efforts from Wake Forest, Florida State and Wake Forest have all come via the passing attack. Although Notre Dame picked up a comfortable victory over Navy, the Irish struggled to find an offensive rhythm in the first half. Head coach Marcus Freeman oversees an offense that's sixth in first-half scoring, as the Notre Dame offense woke up in the second half for 21 points. Both Nolan James Jr. and Jonaz Walton have been the primary contributors to a ground game that ranks top-15 in Success Rate. James has seen an increase in yardage over four straight games, logging more than 100 yards on nine carries against Navy . The biggest Havoc-maker on the defense returned after an ejection during the BYU game. Edge Boubacar Traore should be well rested after missing parts of the last two games, entering Week 10 with 22 pressures on the season. Defensive coordinator Chris Ash has produced one of the best rush-stopping units while ranking ninth in PFF coverage grading. A heavy amount of Cover 1 hasn't exposed Notre Dame in the explosives department , as the Irish have allowed just six rushing attempts that exceeded 20 yards . There's no expectation that Miami's defense will be able to stop Notre Dame's passing attack, led by quarterback CJ Carr. The Hurricanes have struggled against ACC quarterbacks with low national rankings. UNC's Billy Edwards Jr. and Florida State's Ashton Daniels combined for eight touchdowns against the Canes. Clemson's Tait Reynolds also exceeded his season high by a mile, posting 294 passing yards against Miami. The issue for the Hurricanes comes in the middle of the defense, as teams have exploited the pass mid-range between the hash marks . A number of Miami starters have bottom-P4 grades in coverage, including linebacker Mohamed Toure, cornerback Omar Thornton and a pair of safeties in Zechariah Poyser and JJ Dunnigan. Carr should have success throwing over the middle, particularly to slot Jaden Greathouse. More than 50% of Greathouse's targets have come from 0-9 yards between the hashes. The question remains whether the Notre Dame defense has the capability to stop a Miami offense that's the best in FBS in terms of Passing Success Rate. The Irish should have success limiting running back Mark Fletcher Jr., as Notre Dame produces a negative EPA against teams using man, power and inside zone run concepts. The key to the pass defense comes from the high safety position with Adon Shuler and Luke Talich. Notre Dame has shutdown cornerbacks, none better than Jayden Sanders and Leonard Moore, who have a combined 11 forced incompletions. Shuler and Talich will be responsible for covering Toney over the middle and limiting missed tackles . Talich ranks as the seventh-best defender in space, missing five tackles all season. There's no doubt Miami will respond on offense, but the Notre Dame offense will have success picking apart the middle of the Hurricanes' pass coverage. Both teams have the numbers to suggest multiple drives will end in scoring position, but Notre Dame ranks as the best FBS offense in terms of Finishing Drives. Look for Miami's consistent issues against the pass — and its bottom-10 tackle grade — to be the difference in South Bend. Pick: Notre Dame -5.5 or Better · CJ Carr 21+ Completions (-118) · Jaden Greenhouse Over 40.5 Yards

Initially, then-Tide head coach Nick Saban had said he would be out for one to two weeks with an ankle sprain. away.headline: Miami gets concerning Malachi Toney injury update ahead of Notre Dame clash
away.blurb: Miami will undoubtedly want Toney available for this crucial matchup, but playing through an ankle injury could bring risks for one of the Hurricanes’ most valuable offensive weapons. The undefeated Miami Hurricanes face a major test this weekend when they battle the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in a showdown between College Football Playoff contenders. Miami enters the matchup ranked No. 1 in both the AP Top 25 poll and the initial CFP rankings. Much of that has been thanks to the on-field brilliance of quarterback Darian Mensah and star wide receiver Malachi Toney. However, a concerning injury update regarding Toney surfaced on Wednesday, potentially putting his availability for the Notre Dame matchup in jeopardy. According to ESPN’s Pete Thamel , sources told him and Max Olson that the Hurricanes’ Toney is dealing with an ankle injury, leaving his status for Saturday’s matchup “uncertain.” “Toney is expected to press and attempt to play, given the magnitude of the game,” Thamel also said in his X report. More news: CFP Committee Chair Under Fire for Alabama’s Controversial Ranking Toney ranks second in NCAA football with 73 receptions, third with 1,027 receiving yards, and third with 13 touchdowns. The 5-foot-11 sophomore has delivered several impressive performances this past season, including 154 yards and two touchdowns in Miami’s double-overtime win over Florida State. As of this writing, Toney is also considered one of the leading Heisman Trophy contenders. Mensah has emerged as the favorite to win, and Toney’s production has played a significant role in the quarterback’s success this season. Saturday’s game carries major CFP implications for Miami and Notre Dame. Both teams appeared in the initial CFP rankings, with Miami holding the top spot and Notre Dame landing at No. 11. However, several games remain on their schedules before the playoff field is finalized. A loss could seriously damage Notre Dame’s chances of getting into the College Football Playoff. Meanwhile, Miami is undefeated, and a loss could hurt its standing in the CFP rankings. Keeping that perfect record could strengthen Miami’s chances of a first-round bye in the CFP. The Miami Hurricanes take on the Notre Dame Fighting Irish at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 7. As of this writing, Toney is also considered one of the leading Heisman Trophy contenders. Mensah has emerged as the favorite to win, and Toney’s production has played a significant role in the quarterback’s success this season. Saturday’s game carries major CFP implications for Miami and Notre Dame. Both teams appeared in the initial CFP rankings, with Miami holding the top spot and Notre Dame landing at No. 11. However, several games remain on their schedules before the playoff field is finalized. A loss could seriously damage Notre Dame’s chances of getting into the College Football Playoff. Meanwhile, Miami is undefeated, and a loss could hurt its standing in the CFP rankings. Keeping that perfect record could strengthen Miami’s chances of a first-round bye in the CFP. home.headline: Why Bill O’Brien Hopes Boston College Captain Michael Crounse Returns Against Notre Dame
home.blurb: CHESTNUT HILL, Mass. — The morning after Boston College football’s initial student-athlete availability report for Saturday’s contest against FSU came out, head coach Bill O’Brien spoke on the injury designation for Michael Crounse, the Eagles’ starting center and a prized team captain. The impact Crounse has for BC is paramount for a variety of reasons — that could be seen when he made his return from injury against Georgia Tech in Week 8 , as the Eagles ran for nearly 400 yards. But in BC’s Week 9 loss on the road to Duke , his lower leg got rolled on quite badly in the second half, which forced him out of the game and into a boot. “I mean, he’s progressing,” said O’Brien. “He was in a boot. He’s out of the boot already. So we’ll see for Notre Dame. [I] really, really want him to play against Notre Dame.” While Crounse is officially out this week, the Eagles’ road contest in South Bend, Ind., next week against the Fighting Irish will be a particularly special one for the redshirt junior. Boston College Football Tight End Kaelan Chudzinski Confirmed Available for Duke Game But the main reason that he makes such a big difference on the field stems from his veteran presence in the huddle, which is undeniably a key trait in all levels of sport, especially football. After suffering a knee injury in the Eagles’ Week 1 loss at Cincinnati, Crounse missed four straight games before returning against the Yellow Jackets, and he finished that game without any major setbacks. O’Brien technically confirmed it isn’t a season-ending injury, which is positive news for the Eagles. But it will at least sideline him for this week’s matchup, and possibly one that has been marked on Crounse’s calendar for months. That is because Crounse’s father, Mike, played for Notre Dame from 1986-90, highlighted by a consensus national championship in an undefeated 12-0 1988 season. “It’s a special game for him,” O’Brien said. “But there’s not much we can do about it. We feel terrible for Mike, but it is what it is.” Freshman DJ Williams, who has a 48.7 offensive grade on PFF (Pro Football Focus), which ranks near the very bottom of FBS centers that qualify for a grade, will be making his fifth-career start in Crounse’s place. It is not an ideal situation to be thrust into as an underclassmen, especially as a replacement for a captain of all people. But Williams now has enough experience under his belt to enter Saturday’s showdown with the Seminoles carrying a bit more confidence than he had at the beginning of the season, when he was essentially tossed straight into the ring of fire with no legitimate playing time to lean on as a guidance tool. “DJ’s got another opportunity,” O’Brien said. “And DJ’s had a good week. DJ’s a great dude, and he’s a really good guy who’s practiced very well.” Follow us on Twitter/X , Facebook , YouTube , Instagram , and Tiktok for the latest Boston College news. Our Staff Picks and Final Scores Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS No. 10 Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2) and No. 2 Georgia (7-1, 5-1) are set to square off on Saturday , in what will mark one of the biggest and most consequential games in the history of Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. In order to maintain control of its College Football Playoff destiny, Ole Miss will have to knock off Georgia for the third time in the program’s last four matchups. With a loss, the Rebels will put their season resume in the hands of the playoff committee with little optimism of returning to meaningful postseason play. Considering what Ole Miss has left in the final quarter of its season, there would be a lot of ground to make up. Ahead of the Rebels' top-10 matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Ole Miss Rebels On SI Staff Predictions Oct 18, 2025; Athens, Georgia, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) runs the ball for a touchdown against Mississippi Rebels defensive tackle Will Echoles (52) during the first half of the game at Sanford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matt Galatzan Matt Galatzan The last two times these two teams met, both games were absolute cinema. Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels offense was unstoppable in both matchups, particularly in Round 2, when they knocked of the Bulldogs in the College Football Playoff. This year, the calculus has changed a bit. The Rebels have a new play caller, and new weapons on the outside. The Defense has also been struggling as of late. On the other side, the Bulldogs are built on defense, running the football and controlling the clock - exactly where Ole Miss has been exploited defensively. For Ole Miss to win here, I think Chambliss - especially without Kewan Lacy in the lineup - is going to have to be Superman. We have seen him do it before plenty of times, but if the Bulldogs can deploy a similar game plan that Texas did two weeks ago, it could be a long day. Shekai Mills-Knight could be an X-factor, but it's hard to be able to rely on a redshirt freshman on a stage like this. The Rebels do have an elite home field advantage, but at the end of the day, I think it all comes down to the Rebels defense and if they can hold up against the Georgia run game. I'll take the Dawgs in a tight one. Georgia 31, Ole Miss 27 Understandably, almost everyone had the LSU game circled on Ole Miss’ schedule going into the season. Offensively, Trinidad Chambliss will need to play a game similar to the one he played against LSU all the way back in Week 3. The version of Chambliss we saw against Auburn was the next closest thing, and he’ll have to continue adding yards with his legs even on plays that aren’t broken down. That should translate into a motivated team and an electric environment in Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, and when playing in The Vaught, especially at night, there isn’t a team in the country I’d take over Ole Miss. The Rebels are 26-1 at home since 2023, including a victory over the Bulldogs in the 2024 regular season that had very similar stakes as this game. Picking any team, let alone one that’s been as hot and cold as Ole Miss has been at times this season, to beat the No. 2 team in the country could age poorly. Despite that, give me Pete Golding, Trinidad Chambliss and the rest of the Ole Miss Rebels to win and keep their playoff and SEC Championship ambitions alive and send the Rebel fans home happy on Saturday night. Kirby Smart’s side will never go down easy, and Gunnar Stockton is a solid leader for the Bulldogs offense. Sparks will fly in Oxford, but a repeat of 2024 is in order. My Georgia vs. Ole Miss prediction and college football picks expect Kirby Smart's defense to rise to the occasion this time against Trinidad Chambliss as the Bulldogs seek revenge for last year's Sugar Bowl loss to the Rebels. Georgia is a 3.5-point road favorite as it visits Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Miss., on Saturday, Nov. 7, and kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. TOP PICK Who will win Georgia vs Ole Miss today: Georgia -3.5 Georgia and Ole Miss played two wild shootouts last year, with the Bulldogs winning the regular-season matchup and the Rebels taking it in the Sugar Bowl. This time around, I like Georgia to cover as many as 6.5 points on the road against Ole Miss. Defense will be the difference in the matchup this year, with Georgia having one of the best in the country ( ranked No. 2 by SP+ ), and Ole Miss' being one of the worst in the SEC. With the Rebels down All-American running back Kewan Lacy , the Bulldogs' defense can lock in on stopping Trinidad Chambliss . Chambliss has faced one other defense ranked top five by SP+, Texas , and struggled in a loss. Against the Longhorns, he threw three interceptions and put up a season-low 60% adjusted completion percentage. Georgia vs Ole Miss Over/Under pick: Under 56.5 Though both games between these teams last year were full of points, Georgia's defense should keep it relatively low-scoring this time around, and I would play the Under at 55.5 or better . The Bulldogs' defense ranks top 20 nationally in available yards percentage (33.5%) , havoc rate (19.4%), and success rate allowed (35.2%). With no Lacy for Ole Miss, it'll put even more on Chambliss, who has frequently had to carry the team this season, and we saw that approach fall flat against Texas. However, Georgia's offense hasn't been lighting up the scoreboard lately either, averaging just 23.6 points per game in its last three outings. So while this is one of the must-watch matchups in my Week 10 Top 25 predictions , it's not because I'm expecting another shootout. Georgia vs Ole Miss combo Ole Miss is a feast-or-famine type of team. The Rebels beat LSU and Missouri , but were blown out by Florida and fell behind so quickly against Texas that they couldn't dig themselves out. That's what happens when you lean so heavily on a star QB to make up for an inconsistent run game and one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Against Georgia, Chambliss won't be Superman; Smart has too much NFL talent on a defense that's allowed more than 20 points just once this season. Ole Miss, meanwhile, enters as a +3.5 underdog and is +142 on the moneyline to pull off the upset. The over/under sits at 56.5 total points. The Bulldogs executed against Florida, as the defense limited the Gators to no methodical or explosive drives. Florida gained only half of the national average in available yards, was stuffed on over half of 24 rushing attempts and was limited to converting just 4-of-12 attempts on third down. Defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann has a top-20 defense in nearly every category, including a mark of 19th in pass rush. Georgia sends one of the lowest numbers of defenders on blitzes, typically utilizing just four defenders . The success of sending only four rushers allows at least seven other players to drop into coverage. Offensively, quarterback Gunner Stockton rebounded from three turnovers against Auburn and didn't fumble or throw an interception against Florida. Stockton has created just five turnover-worthy plays this season, all coming in two games against Alabama and Auburn. Both the Crimson Tide and Tigers play a heavy amount of Cover 3, a concept Stockton has produced a modest 52% Success Rate against with a minimal negative EPA. Georgia may not have issues pushing the ball downfield, as Ole Miss has mid-FBS success with quarters and a low 42% pivoting to Cover 3 . The absence of star running back Kewan Lacy was not an issue for Ole Miss , who dominated Auburn in Week 9 with three rushing touchdowns. Makhi Frazier continues to get more attempts with his 5.3 yards per carry, but Shekai Mills-Knight busted out in only his second appearance of the season. The sophomore accounted for a rushing touchdown with three gains over 10 yards and has a season total of 4.5 yards after first contact. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss also continued his Heisman campaign , adding another three touchdowns to an all-purpose total of 25 on the season. Despite the low score, Auburn found a way to push the ball down the field on the Ole Miss defense. In 11 offensive possessions, the Tigers accumulated three explosive drives and four methodical drives while averaging 4.5 overall yards per play. Where Ole Miss played the best defense was in the red zone, as four Auburn trips resulted in just a single touchdown. The Rebels have shown the ability to stop the rush against opponents this season, ranking top-20 in Stuff Rate. Ole Miss continues to struggle in several defensive areas, from pass coverage to tackling and allowing explosives on passing downs. There are a number of reasons to believe the Ole Miss defense won't have success in stopping Georgia. The Rebels sit outside the top 100 in penalties and third-down defense, a massive issue for a unit that's 119th in passing down explosives allowed. The best attribute of the Ole Miss defense comes against the run, but the Rebels have yet to face an inside zone attack that uses 12 personnel like Georgia . Man blocking assignments have been led by running back Nate Frazier, who's fully healed from a rib injury and averaged 5.6 yards per carry against Auburn. Ole Miss has been putrid against man blocking with a low 43% Success Rate. Containing Chambliss is priority No. 1 for Georgia. Schumann called defense against Ole Miss twice last season, allowing 44 yards in scrambles. Georgia solved the Chambliss question in a playoff loss, keeping the Ole Miss quarterback from a single scramble. He totaled just 14 yards on designed run calls. Chambliss was assisted by season highs in receiving from both Harrison Wallace III and De'Zhaun Stribling. Ellis Robinson IV has been a shutdown cornerback for the Bulldogs this season and is sure to draw the assignment against Deuce Alexander. Keep tabs on Robinson after a knee injury against Florida, but Smart indicated the news was positive for the corner this week. Action Network's Betting Power Ratings call for Georgia to be a 7.5-point favorite , well ahead of a market favoring the Bulldogs by just 3.5. The Ole Miss defense will be tasked with facing run concepts using a two-tight-end set while overproducing season-average numbers on third downs. Georgia looked healthy in a demolition of Florida after the bye week, resolving any lingering injury issues with Frazier and Stockton. The biggest question is whether or not Chambliss will be allowed to generate first downs on scrambles while connecting downfield. Georgia contained the Chambliss scrambles in the SEC Championship but must show why it's 11th overall in coverage to beat Ole Miss. Pick: Georgia -3.5

away.headline: Georgia football WR Isiah Canion nowhere to be found on UGA's injury report
away.source: Dawn of the Dawg on MSN
away.blurb: Isiah Canion was one of Georgia's biggest acquisitions out of the Transfer Portal this offseason. He came to Georgia after spending two seasons at Georgia Tech, and he was expected to be a central piece of the Bulldogs' passing attack this year. He unfortunately was hurt during the second game of Georgia's season and hasn't seen the field since. Earlier this week though he was marked probable to play on Georgia's official injury report and on Thursday he was nowhere to be found on their report which means he has been officially cleared to play. This injury update does need to be taken with a grain of salt. Nate Frazier came off Georgia's injury report heading into the Alabama game, but he still didn't play. Based on that it still isn't a 100 percent guarantee that Canion will play against Ole Miss, but he most likely will be available. Chauncey Bowens still questionable to play vs Ole Miss While it looks like Georgia will finally be getting Canion back, the same can't be said for running back Chauncey Bowens. On Thursday's injury report he was still listed as questionable to play, so there is a chance he will be able to suit up against the Rebels. There however is just as good of a chance that he won't be able to play either. Another injury report will come out Friday night before one final injury update about an hour before kickoff on Saturday. Georgia's injured 3-headed monster could all return in time to play Florida Georgia WR Isiah Canion injury update is great news for UGA Canion has only recorded three receptions for 28 yards this season. That can't be held against him though because the starters barely played in Georgia's season opener against Tennessee State before he got hurt the following week in Week 2. Canion has a lot of potential though that Georgia hasn't seen yet. Last year at Georgia Tech he was an integral part of their talented offense as he recorded 33 receptions for 480 yards and four touchdowns. He isn't a player that will ever be the No. 1 target in Georgia's offense, but he can be another reliable option for Gunner Stockton in a game where UGA needs a lot of offense. This is great timing for Georgia because the Ole Miss offense, with quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, dominated UGA the two times they played last season. Georgia's offense likely needs to score a lot of points to win this game, and Canion being back on the field will help them accomplish that. Bowens hasn't played since the Vanderbilt game nearly a month ago. He is Georgia's No. 2 running back who has scored six touchdowns this season, so similarly to Canion the Bulldogs' offense would be at their best with him in the lineup against Ole Miss. Georgia thankfully has plenty of pieces in their running back room to make up for Bowens if he isn't able to play this weekend. away.blurb: Friday Ole Miss vs. Georgia Injury Report: Keaton Thomas Probable - The Rebel Walk FRIDAY Ole Miss vs. Georgia Injury Report: Keaton Thomas Probable, Franklin Questionable Recent ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – Ole Miss linebacker Keaton Thomas is probable for Saturday night's game against No. 2 Georgia after being questionable on Thursday, according to the SEC's Friday availability report. Defensive end Kam Franklin remains questionable. The report was posted at 7:10 p.m. CT on Friday. Ole Miss' list of players who are out did not change, with running back Kewan Lacy and eight others ruled out again. Georgia, meanwhile, moved three players from questionable to out: inside linebacker AJ Kruah , safety Tyriq Green and defensive lineman Joseph Jonah-Ajonye . Keaton Thomas moves up to probable Thomas, a linebacker, was questionable on both Wednesday and Thursday and is now probable for Saturday night. That is the only change to the Ole Miss availability designations from Thursday. Cornerback Jalyn Crawford and safety MJ Preston remain probable, and no other Rebels are listed. Kam Franklin remains questionable Franklin has carried the questionable tag all week and has not been cleared with kickoff about 23 hours away. He has 25 tackles, including 15 solo stops and 10 assists, along with 5.0 tackles for loss, two sacks, a pass breakup and a fumble recovery he returned for a touchdown through eight games this season. He was named a leader of the defense in our September feature on Franklin . Without him, Ole Miss would lose one of its best pass rushers and run stoppers against a Georgia offense that scores 41 points per game. Georgia's report got shorter on the questionable side and longer on the out side. Kruah, Green and Jonah-Ajonye were all questionable on Thursday and are now out, joining outside linebacker Amaris Williams, who has been out all week. Tight end Elyiss Williams remains questionable. Wide receiver Thomas Blackshear and running back Chauncey Bowens were questionable Thursday and are now probable. OU will win a game and lose the next before winning again. Colton Sulley, OU beat writer Florida 27, OU 19 The Sooners keep it a one-score game with a plethora of Gators likely out. But Witten isn't able to fix all of OU's offensive issues quite yet. Jacob Unruh, deputy sports editor Florida 23, OU 20 Changing offensive coordinators is not enough to fix all of the issues the Sooners have on that side of the ball, even if a quarterback change is made. But some improvement is better than none. The issue is trying to make those changes in The Swamp while hoping an elite defense that showed signs of wearing down can rebound. picks.headline: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida?
picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? Oklahoma Sooners tight ends coach Jason Witten will take over as interim offensive coordinator for the rest of the season. | Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Gators have an impressive resume, having beaten No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28 at The Swamp, then going on the road to Austin and taking down No. 7 Texas 27-24 - one week after OU beat them in Dallas - on a night the underwhelming Florida defense overwhelmed Arch Manning and the Longhorns, sacking him five times, limiting UT to 2-of-10 on third down (they had 13 first downs total) and holding the Horns to 272 total yards. But they were also blown out in back-to-back losses to No. 25 Missouri and unranked South Carolina, which preceded last week's 27-8 loss to No. 3 Georgia. Oklahoma is a touchdown underdog to Florida, but the Sooners are the best defense the Gators face. Still, OU may be reeling after its worst defensive performance in years in the blowout loss to South Carolina - which included an incomprehensible 25 missed tackles (usually 10 is a bad number). OU's first trip to The Swamp will be punctuated by another big game from Gators RB Jaden Baugh, who's third in the SEC at 100.3 rushing yards per game and first with 13 rushing TDs. Final score: Florida 28, Oklahoma 21 Things could get gross Saturday night. Florida has officially made a quarterback change, and Tramell Jones Jr. could be without a pair of key weapons to pair with an already banged up offensive line. Oklahoma's offense has been so bad it got its coordinator fired, but Jason Witten has never called plays collegiately and John Mateer is still likely the quarterback the Sooners will roll with. OU's defense needs to bounce back after its tackling struggles last week, but even an improved showing could see Gator running back Jaden Baugh have enough success to push Jon Sumrall's team across the finish line. Final: Florida 16, Oklahoma 13 OU is set up for further disaster as it heads to the swamp. Jason Witten will serve as the Sooners' play caller for the first time at the college level, John Mateer is still the quarterback and Ben Hill Griffin Stadium is one of the nation's most hostile atmospheres. But amid the weirdness, I expect OU to win this game. Teams often come out more inspired after a notable firing, and I predict Witten will lead a creative game plan as he auditions for the full-time offensive coordinator role. Florida's offense is good - but it is also prone to turning the ball over. If the Sooners are able to put pressure on Tramell Jones Jr. early, it will create a long day for the Gators' offense. Final: Oklahoma 24, Florida 20 The Sooners figure to get a little boost from Jason Witten's playcalling, but don't expect massive changes in either scheme or production here. The offensive line still has its issues, John Mateer hasn't been consistent at all, and neither of the other quarterbacks have experience in games like this. But Oklahoma's defense does figure to have a bounce-back game after struggling to contain LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina offense. The tackling will be better, and Florida's offense is in a bit of flux itself with Tramell Jones Jr. expected to make his second start of the season at quarterback and Florida's offensive line struggling in recent weeks. But the Gators still have plenty of talent, especially on the offensive side, and The Swamp is one of the toughest environments in college football. That's a tough position for a reeling team to be placed in. The game will be close into the second half but the Gators figure to pull away and hand Oklahoma its second consecutive defeat. Final: Florida 24, Oklahoma 14 Brady Trantham A new offensive coordinator doesn'tchange the fact that John Mateer is still QB1 at OU. Mateer gives Oklahoma their best shot in any game, but in 20 games as the Sooner signal caller, it is apparent that he simply isn't very good. A coaching change can, in theory, help him in spots, but if OU needs their QB to make a play in a tight game, chances are he will make that play - just for the other team. Florida sticks to the run and gets Oklahoma on a few explosives and rides it to an easy win. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Sat, November 7, 2026 at 2:18 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When we last saw Oklahoma and Florida play, the Sooners rolled 55-20 in the 2020 Cotton Bowl over a high-powered Gator team that lost to eventual national champion Alabama in an epic SEC Championship. The other meeting was the BCS Championship at the end of the 2009 season, when Tim Tebow and the Gator defense took down Heisman-winner Sam Bradford and the amazing Sooner attack 24-14 for the national title. The stakes aren't as high this time around, but for a Florida program that's on the rise, and No. 24 in the first College Football Playoff rankings, and for a 4-4 Oklahoma desperate to close strong, this will be intense. Oklahoma vs Florida: Quick Hits Oklahoma at 4-4, needs to win two of its last four to be bowl eligible. It hosts Ole Miss and Texas A&M after this before closing at Missouri. Florida is coming off the 27-8 loss to Georgia. It goes to Kentucky next, hosts Vanderbilt, and finishes at Florida State. Again, the first two meetings were in big bowl games. This is the first regular season matchup between the two. How To Watch Oklahoma vs Florida Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 7:45 PM ET TV: SEC Network Location: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville, FL – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Oklahoma Will Win The defense continues to fight the good fight. It had a problem in the 42-25 loss to South Carolina, but the defense is fantastic on third downs thanks to a pass rush that takes over games. But to beat Florida, you have to slow down the run. The Gators are 0-3 when running for fewer than 155 yards, and the Sooners give up just 107 yards per game. Only Mississippi State and, last week, South Carolina have been able to gash the Sooners for more. Why Florida Will Win Oklahoma's offense has a hard time running the ball. With a defense as good as the Sooners have, all the O has to do is keep it moving and not screw it up. But no running game means more pressing overall, and then come the mistakes. The Sooners only average 107 yards per game on the ground, and they just can't find any room to move. The Gators have to hold up, and then pounce on an Oklahoma attack that turned it over four times against both Georgia and Kentucky, three times against New Mexico, and twice against Michigan. Oklahoma vs Florida Prediction, Betting Lines It's stupid, but if you buy into these things, going back to the last two games of last season, Oklahoma is on a ten-game run of alternating wins and losses. The Sooners beat Texas, then lost to Kentucky, beat Mississippi State, lost to South Carolina, beat … Florida? The Sooners have the defense to hold up and make Florida struggle. The Gators got by Texas a few weeks ago, but it's been a struggle, losing three of the last four. Weird trends aside, this Oklahoma team really does have a way of rallying when it absolutely has to.
