picks.headline: Florida vs. Oklahoma Final Score Predictions: Experts predict fascinating battle between two traditional powers with QB issues
picks.blurb: Florida vs. Oklahoma Final Score Predictions: Experts predict fascinating battle between two traditional powers with QB issues - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Scott Wachter-Imagn Images, BRYAN TERRY/THE OKLAHOMAN-Imagn Images Brandon Little, Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness · AtoZ Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Florida Gators and Oklahoma Sooners meet for the first time in SEC play, and both teams have questions at quarterback. The Florida Gators and Oklahoma Sooners are set to meet for just the third time in history on Saturday night, and it will be the first game in The Swamp. In the history of both programs, they have met twice: 2008 BCS National Championship Game (Florida won 24- 14) and 2020 Cotton Bowl (Oklahoma won 55-20). This year, it will be a much different game than both before it, as both quarterback spots are in a tough spot. The Gators have a quarterback controversy with Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr., while Oklahoma has had numerous issues with John Mateer, leading to the dismissal of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle. Who will get the win and take one step forward? It's primed to be a great game, and our experts predicted the game. Florida 20, Oklahoma 9 It was disappointing to see the Gators fail to take advantage of their impressive defensive performance against the Georgia Bulldogs, but it was two consecutive plus performances for a unit that has been rough this season. Now you give that unit John Mateer with Jason Witten calling plays for the first time? This could be a disaster for the Sooners. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Florida 34, Oklahoma 13 Florida likely saw their playoff hopes extinguished last weekend against Georgia, but they've got a golden opportunity to get right on Saturday at home against Oklahoma. The Sooners fired offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle after a blowout home loss to South Carolina, and there's no reason to believe that things are going to improve on the road against a Gators defense that held Georgia relatively in check offensively last week. Jadan Baugh and the Gators get things rolling early, and Oklahoma lacks the horses to keep this a game by mid-third quarter. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Florida 21, Oklahoma 10 This game is going to be a grind, with neither offense finding much consistency throughout the afternoon. Oklahoma's defense will do its part to keep the Sooners in it, making life difficult for the Gators and keeping the score within one possession for much of the game. But John Mateer and the Oklahoma offense continue to look like a major problem. The Sooners struggle to sustain drives, miss opportunities and put too much pressure on their defense to carry the load. Florida won't exactly light up the scoreboard either, but the Gators will do enough to eventually pull away. Their defense should take advantage of Oklahoma's offensive struggles, while the offense finds just enough success to put points on the board. The game stays uncomfortably close into the fourth quarter before Florida puts together a late scoring drive to finally seal it. It won't be pretty, but the Gators will take it. Florida wins 21-10. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Florida 27, Oklahoma 20 This game features two teams on opposite ends of the preseason spectrum. Yes, the Gators have 3 losses heading into November, but they have some of the best wins in the conference after beating Ole Miss and Texas. The Gators look to be in good hands with Jon Sumrall for years to come, as he has exceeded all year-one expectations. For OU, things couldn't have gone more wrong. John Mateer regressed, the offense has been horrific, and OC Ben Arbuckle was just let go this week. Still, the defense and Brent Venables will create trouble for a Florida Gators offense that can look like one of the best in the country one week, and a mess the next. But catching the Sooners in the swamp will be a win for Florida. I expect Jadan Baugh and the defense to do enough to prevent the new OC bump for the Sooners. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Florida 23, Oklahoma 17 Florida is coming off a blowout loss to Georgia that'll have them wanting to get right at home. Oklahoma making staff changes could result in some early juice from the Sooners' offense, as we sometimes see with programs after a big change. However, I think the Gators are going to move to 6-3 and keep alive what has been a solid first season for Jon Sumrall in Gainesville. The QB situation is going to matter against a talented Oklahoma defense, but the Gators will figure it out. – Brandon Little , A to Z Ohio State Final Prediction for Florida vs. Oklahoma To nobody's surprise, our experts are in favor of the Gators here. The Sooners are in a really tough spot, and a trip to The Swamp with a first-time play caller isn't likely to help any. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.blurb: Young, who was not on the initial player availability report on Wednesday, was listed by Oklahoma State as probable going into the game on Saturday against Kansas State. Kickoff is set for noon, and the game will be broadcast on TNT. Young joined safety Quentin Hammonds, who was listed as probable on the report on Wednesday. Hammonds suffered an injury against Colorado but recovered in time to play against Iowa State. Three Cowboys remain doubtful for the game — defensive end Jaleel Johnson, linebacker Tate Romney and defensive lineman Landon Dean. Johnson and Romney both suffered injuries during the Iowa State game. Dean suffered an injury that forced him to miss games earlier this season but returned to the lineup. Wide receiver Dayvon Standard was added to the report as out, alongside tight end Carson Kolb, who is dealing with a foot injury that Morris said could keep him out another week or two. As for the Wildcats, their report remained the same as Wednesday, except for the addition of linebacker Sawyer Schilke, who is now questionable. OUT : TE Carson Kolb, WR Dayvon Standard DOUBTFUL : LB Tate Romney, DT Landon Dean, DE Jaleel Johnson PROBABLE : S Quinton Hammonds, WR Wyatt Young OUT : QB Avery Johnson, QB Jacob Knuth QUESTIONABLE : S Koy Beasley, RB Jay Harris, LB DJ Ackerson Jr., TE Lawson McGraw, DT Eli Jackson, LB Sawyer Schilke. Oklahoma State Lists Tate Romney, Jaleel Johnson as Doubtful for Kansas State Game The Oklahoma State Cowboys made a surprise adjustment to their player availability report on Thursday — wide receiver Wyatt Young. Young played the entire game against Iowa State last weekend and head coach Eric Morris did not give any indication that Young's status was in question going into the Kansas State game. OSU, K-State Updated Injury Report Young is coming off a game in which he scored twice against the Cyclones but committed a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty after the second touchdown catch, which put the Cowboys ahead, 49-48, in the final minute of the game. After the game, Young posted an apology to Oklahoma State fans on social media, texted his head coach to apologize and apologized to his teammates. away.blurb: Off a disappointing loss to Georgia, the Florida Gators (5-3, 3-3 SEC) return home to face Oklahoma (4-4. 2-3 SEC) at The Swamp on Saturday, November 7 (7:45 p.m., SEC Network). The 6-0, 196-pound Jones is 1-0 as a starter, leading Florida o a 27-24 upset win at Texas on October 17 when Philo was out with a shoulder injury. The Gators will be down one starter on the line as right tackle Emeka Ugorji has been ruled out for the Oklahoma game. That opens up an opportunity for 6-8, 319-pound right tackle Caden Jones, who made 10 starts for the Gators last season. Florida will face a challenge against an Oklahoma defense that ranks fifth in the SEC sacks (23) and seventh in tackles for loss (6.1). The Gators will look to get star running back Jadan Baugh back going, as the 6-1, 225-pound Baugh has failed to rush for more than 100 yards in four straight games. The return of Duke Clark, who has been out close to a month due to injury, also could help spark the run game. "We've been trusting each other a lot better than what we have in the past. I feel like in the past, everybody was playing out of sync almost in a way," Florida defensive lineman Brendan Bett said. "But these last few games, I think we kind of just locked arms and just really trusted each other to compete and execute and do our jobs at an elite level." Florida will honor Hall of Fame coach Urban Meyer during the game, inducting him into the stadium's ring of honor. Meyer was involved in the process to hire Sumrall, who is trying to get the Gators back on track after a 1-3 October that included the 27-8 loss to the Bulldogs on Halloween in Atlanta. "Not what we need to do last Saturday as a team," Sumrall said. "We got an opportunity to respond this week, excited about that. A lot of growth is needed within our football team. We're hard at working, getting it done." Here are five storylines to watch in UF's matchup with the Sooners: Can Florida football QB Tramell Jones Jr. provide a spark to the offense? Florida is turning to Jones as starting quarterback after incumbent starter Aaron Philo threw two interceptions and was benched in the first half against Georgia. Jones was able to move the offense in relief of Jones against the Bulldogs, passing for 172 yards and rushing for 17 yards and a TD. "Attribute that to a lot of poise, right, and preparation," Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said. "He knows where everybody he is. There's probably a couple we'd like back, but other than that I thought he did a good job. Got to continue to work, continue to get better." For the season, Jones has passed for 579 yards and 4 TDS while throwing 3 interceptions. He's also added 83 yards and 1 TD rushing. Can Florida football OL raise its level of play to protect Jones and get the run game back going? away.blurb: That is no different against the Florida Gators on Saturday. In the latest availability report , the Sooners have eight players listed as out, one as doubtful, one as questionable and two as probable. The Sooners will be without Ryan Fodje, Cole Sullivan and Jacobe Johnson for sure, as well as likely being without Eddy Pierre-Louis. Peyton Bowen is listed as questionable, so they could be without their star safety. On the bright side, Eli Bowen, Jake Maikkula, Jer'Michael Carter and Rocky Beers are all back this week. The Sooners may also get Elijah Thomas back. The injury situation remains a big concern for Oklahoma as it heads into one of its toughest road environments of the season. Losing a potential difference-maker like Peyton Bowen would be a major blow to the Sooners' secondary, while the absences along the offensive and defensive lines could also test the team's depth. With so many players unavailable, Oklahoma will need contributions from its next group of players to keep Florida's offense in check. Still, the return of several players provides a boost for a team that has struggled to stay healthy throughout the season. Getting Eli, Maikkula, Carter and Beers back gives the Sooners more options, and Thomas could provide another welcome addition if he is cleared to play. Oklahoma will need every available contribution as it looks to overcome its injury challenges and leave Gainesville with a win. away.headline: Oklahoma Sooners starting offensive lineman trending toward return
away.blurb: Maikkula missed the South Carolina game with a lower-body injury suffered in the win over Mississippi State. As long as he maintains his probable status over the next couple of days, Maikkula will likely return to the starting lineup for the Sooners' road trip to face the Florida Gators . If he does, it'll be the most intact the Oklahoma offensive line has been this season after Heath Ozaeta returned to the starting lineup last weekend. The other big name to watch for the Sooners offense is tight end Rocky Beers. Beers is Oklahoma's second-leading receiver this season, with 34 receptions for 446 yards, and leads the team with four receiving touchdowns. Beers was listed as questionable for this Saturday. If he's not able to play, Hayden Hansen will get a vast majority of the tight end snaps, but the Sooners will need someone to step up in the pass-catching department. Also of note are the questionable tags on defensive backs Peyton and Eli Bowen. Peyton played last week against South Carolina, while Eli missed his fourth game in a row. Against a talented Florida wide receiver group, the Sooners defense would certainly benefit from their availability on Saturday. Florida will be without starting offensive tackle Emeka Ugorji this week. Two of their better wide receivers in Bailey Stockton (questionable) and Vernell Brown III are also in danger of missing the Week 10 contest. Stockton is second on the Gators in receiving, and Brown is third. Brown hasn't played since late September. Another name to keep an eye on is defensive end Emmanuel Oyebadejo. Oyebadejo is tied for the team lead with 4.5 sacks and is second in tackles for loss. He's also listed as questionable this week. home.headline: Florida has 7 players on initial SEC Availability Report for Week 10
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: Four Gators are listed as out: defensive lineman Jeramiah McCloud, tight end Evan Chieca, offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji and linebacker Jaden Robinson. McCloud is out due to a suspension, according to Swamp247 , while Robinson missed his first game of the season last week against Georgia. Listed as doubtful is wide receiver Vernell Brown III, who has missed the last four games with a grade-1 PCL strain that he suffered against Ole Miss in Week 4 that was re-aggravated ahead of last week's Georgia game. "So he was not available at practice today," Jon Sumrall said on Monday . "I really don't have a really strong feeling on timeline because everything early in the week last week was trending really positively until the setback on Wednesday. It sucks. It sucks for him. He's working like hell to try to get back. He's frustrated." The two players listed as questionable are wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo. Stockton has been dealing with a nagging foot injury but still played against the Bulldogs last week, finishing with 76 yards on eight catches. Wide receiver Elijah Thomas and offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis are listed as doubtful, while wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, defensive backs Peyton Bowen and Eli Bowen, tight end Rocky Beers and defensive lineman Kenny Ozowalu are listed as questionable, and offensive lineman Jake Maikkula is listed as probable. WR Bailey Stockton — questionable DL Emmanuel Oyebadejo — questionable OL Eddy Pierre-Louis — doubtful WR Jer'Michael Carter — questionable DL Kenny Ozowalu — questionable OL #69 Jake Maikkula — probable Questionable (50% chance to play) The initial SEC availability report for college football's Week 10 was released on Wednesday night; the Florida Gators have seven players listed, while the Oklahoma Sooners have a whopping 16. "Jeramiah McCloud has been suspended for this week's game against Oklahoma for conduct detrimental to the team. His status with the program will be re-evaluated after this week's contest," per a statement from a program spokesperson. Sumrall added what he called his "official VB3 statement": "He wants to play. He's doing everything he can to play. He's pissed off he can't play, and he's doing everything in his power to play. It's a real injury that we thought we were on the other side of that he had a setback last week, and it sucks. I mean, it freaking sucks for him." Oklahoma has eight players who are not expected to play on Saturday: linebacker Taylor Heim, defensive back Dakoda Fields, wide receiver Trell Harris, linebacker Cole Sullivan, tight end Trynae Washington, defensive back Jacobe Johnson, and offensive linemen Ryan Fodje and Fred Hinton. home.headline: Scouting report, prediction as Florida football hosts Oklahoma
home.blurb: Off a disappointing loss to Georgia, the Florida Gators (5-3, 3-3 SEC) return home to face Oklahoma (4-4. 2-3 SEC) at The Swamp on Saturday, November 7 (7:45 p.m., SEC Network). The 6-0, 196-pound Jones is 1-0 as a starter, leading Florida o a 27-24 upset win at Texas on October 17 when Philo was out with a shoulder injury. The Gators will be down one starter on the line as right tackle Emeka Ugorji has been ruled out for the Oklahoma game. That opens up an opportunity for 6-8, 319-pound right tackle Caden Jones, who made 10 starts for the Gators last season. Florida will face a challenge against an Oklahoma defense that ranks fifth in the SEC sacks (23) and seventh in tackles for loss (6.1). The Gators will look to get star running back Jadan Baugh back going, as the 6-1, 225-pound Baugh has failed to rush for more than 100 yards in four straight games. The return of Duke Clark, who has been out close to a month due to injury, also could help spark the run game. "We've been trusting each other a lot better than what we have in the past. I feel like in the past, everybody was playing out of sync almost in a way," Florida defensive lineman Brendan Bett said. "But these last few games, I think we kind of just locked arms and just really trusted each other to compete and execute and do our jobs at an elite level." Florida will honor Hall of Fame coach Urban Meyer during the game, inducting him into the stadium's ring of honor. Meyer was involved in the process to hire Sumrall, who is trying to get the Gators back on track after a 1-3 October that included the 27-8 loss to the Bulldogs on Halloween in Atlanta. "Not what we need to do last Saturday as a team," Sumrall said. "We got an opportunity to respond this week, excited about that. A lot of growth is needed within our football team. We're hard at working, getting it done." Here are five storylines to watch in UF's matchup with the Sooners: Can Florida football QB Tramell Jones Jr. provide a spark to the offense? Florida is turning to Jones as starting quarterback after incumbent starter Aaron Philo threw two interceptions and was benched in the first half against Georgia. Jones was able to move the offense in relief of Jones against the Bulldogs, passing for 172 yards and rushing for 17 yards and a TD. "Attribute that to a lot of poise, right, and preparation," Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said. "He knows where everybody he is. There's probably a couple we'd like back, but other than that I thought he did a good job. Got to continue to work, continue to get better." For the season, Jones has passed for 579 yards and 4 TDS while throwing 3 interceptions. He's also added 83 yards and 1 TD rushing. Can Florida football OL raise its level of play to protect Jones and get the run game back going?
